literature.summary:
Finished 20:20 EST. Sources were read as TeX (arXiv e-print), not abstracts. Verbatim prose is kept to one short quote; formulas are transcribed faithfully and line numbers are given so the exact text can be re-read.

A. DIRECTION CONFIRMED (BRS, "Adding one random real", arXiv:math/9406229, J. Symbolic Logic 61 (1996) 80-90; TeX lines 289-307).
Theorem 1.1, headed "[Pawlikowski, Krawczyk]", says that in V^B (B = measure algebra for one random real):
(1) add(N) = add(N)^V, cof(N) = cof(N)^V; (2) cov(N) >= cov(N)^V, non(N) <= non(N)^V; (3) cov(N) >= b and non(N) <= d; (4) b = b^V, d = d^V; (5) cov(M) >= cov(M)^V, non(M) <= non(M)^V; (6) add(M) >= add(M)^V, cof(M) <= cof(M)^V.
(The source macro \unif prints "non".) So the note's Remark 4 has the right direction: non(N)^{V^B} <= d, cov(N)^{V^B} >= b.
Attribution in the proof line: (1),(2),(4) folklore (see Pawlikowski 1986); "(3) is due to Krawczyk (see [Paw86Sol] or [Kra83])"; (5) due to Pawlikowski; (6) from (5),(4).
Bibliography as printed: [Kra83] Adam Krawczyk, Dominating reals add random reals, 1985, unpublished notes. [Paw86Sol] Janusz Pawlikowski, Why Solovay real produces Cohen real, J. Symbolic Logic 51 (1986), no. 4, 957-968. Note: Pawlikowski's own reference list (Cambridge page) cites Krawczyk as "A note on random reals, handwritten note, 1983". The two citations of Krawczyk disagree in title and year.

B. OTHER RESULTS ON non(N) IN V^B (all fetched).
- BRS Def. 3.1 / Lemma 3.2: non*(N) = non(N)^{V^B}, where non*(N) is the least size of a family X of Borel functions such that for every planar null H and every positive Borel B some f in X has {x in B : (x,f(x)) not in H} non-null.
- BRS Thm 2.1: cov(M), non(M), add(M), cof(M) are unchanged in V^B.
- BRS Thm 3.9: consistent non*(N) < min{non(N), d}. Thm 3.10: consistent non*(N) < b.
- BRS-Shelah follow-up "After all, there are some inequalities which are provable in ZFC" (arXiv:math/9711222, JSL 65 (2000) 803-816), section 3: non*(N) <= lambda* := inf_f b(R^exists_f) = non(SN) (Miller's characterization, cited there); Corollary: non*(N) <= min{d, non(SN)}; Lemma: non*(N) >= cov(M); Lemma: if non*(N) <= b then non*(N) = cov(M). It also restates Krawczyk's theorem: if V∩ω^ω is bounded in V*, and r is random over V*, then V*[r] has a random real over V[r].
- Cardona (arXiv:2109.00736) restates Pawlikowski 1986 Prop. 3.1 in two-model form, including d_N^M => non(N)_{N[r]}^{M[r]} and non(N)_N^M => non(N)_{N[r]}^{M[r]}, and reproves the first as a Tukey connection.
Lower bounds from the literature: non(N)^{V^B} >= max{add(N), cov(M)}. Nothing relates it to b from below (consistently non*(N) < b), and nothing found bounds it below by non(M).

C. CONSEQUENCES FOR g (my derivations; unreviewed).
C1 (proved, one line). g <= non*(N). Proof: if the graphs of all f in X lie in a null H, then with B = whole space every set {x : (x,f(x)) not in H} is empty, so X is not a non*-witness.
Hence g <= non(N)^{V^B} <= min{d, non(SN)}, and g <= cov(M) whenever non*(N) <= b (in particular whenever b = d).
C2 (corollary for the note, given its Theorem). If a UN set of size c exists: add(UN) <= min{d, non(SN)}; and if also b = d then add(UN) <= cov(M). Mathias model: with the values in context.md (b = d = non(N) = c, cov(M) = aleph_1; not re-checked by me) this gives add(UN) = add(N) = aleph_1. So the Mathias model is ruled out. A model of add(N) < add(UN) with a UN set of size c needs add(N) < g <= min{d, non(SN)} and (b < non*(N), hence b < d, or add(N) < cov(M)).
C3 (new, proof sketch below; needs review). In any Cohen extension W = V[C_kappa], the Borel functions coded in V have a non-null union of graphs, so g^W <= (2^{aleph_0})^V. In the Cohen model over CH: g = add(N) = aleph_1 < cov(M) = non*(N) = c. So the parenthetical in context.md, "g should equal non(N) in the one-random-real extension", is false in general; only g <= non(N)^{V^B} holds. Also g >= cov(M) is not a ZFC theorem.
Sketch. Claim A: let G be Polish, z -> T_z continuous into trees with [T_z] of positive measure and T_z equal to its measure support. Then every non-empty open set contains an open O' with a comeager G' ⊆ O' and a continuous injection psi on G' with psi(z) in [T_z]. Proof: by Baire category pick O', sigma with sigma in T_z and relative measure of [T_z] in [sigma] >= 3/4 on O' (these sets are closed by upper semicontinuity; Lebesgue density gives the cover). Recursively split each piece O (string sigma_O) into countably many open pieces O_i with dense union, strings sigma_i extending sigma_O, |sigma_i| >= |sigma_O|+i+2, pairwise incompatible, same 3/4 invariant. Room: earlier siblings use at most half of [sigma_O], the tree keeps at least 3/4, so a density point outside them exists for every z in O; Baire category again gives an open piece. Diameters go to 0; psi(z) is the union of the strings; siblings have incompatible strings, so psi is injective.
Then in V[c] every closed positive-measure P contains x = psi(c) with c = psi^{-1}(x) in V[x]. Given a null H in W covering all V-coded graphs, H is coded in V[c] for one Cohen real c; take compact K of positive measure off H in V[c], x in {x : K_x positive} with c in V[x], y in K_x; y = eta(c) for a V-coded Borel eta, so (x,y) is on the graph of eta∘psi^{-1}, a contradiction.
C4 (open). I found no model with g > add(N) and no proof of g = add(N). Necessary for destroying the witness "all V-coded Borel functions": the extension has a real h with {x : h in V[x]} null (true for an amoeba real; false for a Cohen real by Claim A). Natural test: the Hechler model (add(N) = aleph_1, add(M) = c); Goto's Theorem 5.18 already gives add(UN) = aleph_1 there, so it can only test whether the bound g is sharp. The laver model has g = aleph_1 < b, so g >= b is not a theorem.
Related ZFC fact (abstract only): Cichoń-Pawlikowski show the plane ideal "covered by a Borel set with all vertical sections in I" has an aleph_1-union outside it. This "every section" versus "almost every section" gap is the same gap that separates g from non*(N).

D. Question 6.3 is not answered by this literature. No fetched source mentions add(UN) or the note's Theorem; Goto's paper does not cite BRS, Krawczyk, or Pawlikowski 1986.

findings.exactStatement: For N ⊆ M models, r random over M, c Cohen over M: (R1) add(N) and cof(N) statements are equivalent before and after r; (R2) same for b, d; (R3) d_N^M implies non(N)_{N[r]}^{M[r]}, and cov(N)_{N[r]}^{M[r]} implies b_N^M; (R5) non(N)_N^M implies non(N)_{N[r]}^{M[r]}; (C3) add(N)_N^M implies add(N)_{N[c]}^{M[c]}, which is equivalent to cov(N)_{N[c]}^{M[c]}; (C4) non(N)_{N[c]}^{M[c]} is equivalent to cof(N)_{N[c]}^{M[c]}. Lemma: non(N)_{N[c]}^{M[c]} implies that M has no reals outside N. Quoted Cichoń-Pawlikowski Thm 1.1: a Borel B ⊆ (2^ω)^3 with all sections B_(x,y) null such that for every Borel f the set of x for which {y : f(y) not in B_(x,y)} is non-meager is countable.

Abstract (paraphrase): after adding a Solovay real r and then a Cohen real c to M, M[r][c] contains a Cohen real over M[c]. Full text is paywalled; Proposition 3.1 was not read directly.

findings.relevance: Shows a ZFC aleph_1-additivity phenomenon for plane ideals defined by requiring every vertical section to be small. This is the same every-section versus almost-every-section gap that separates g from non*(N). It does not decide g versus add(N).
findings.exactStatement: Abstract (paraphrase): for a proper ideal I containing the finite sets, let I* be the plane sets contained in a Borel set all of whose vertical sections are in I. There are omega_1 sets in I* whose union is not in I*. The last section treats the null and meager ideals in Cohen extensions.

literature.summary:
Finished 19:59 EST (deadline 20:45). I found no prior statement of the bound "a universally null set of size c exists implies add(UN) <= d", and no answer to Goto's Question 6.3. The search was broad but not complete (see notChecked).

WHAT THE LITERATURE SAYS ABOUT add(UN)
- Only two sources state anything about add(UN). Goto (arXiv:2607.12936v4, still the latest version) proves add(UN,N) = add(UN) and add(N) <= add(UN). Fremlin, Measure Theory vol. 5, 544L(a), already has add(Un) >= add(N) for the universally negligible ideal of any metrizable space. So Goto's Corollary 5.13 is not new, but nothing beyond it is in print.
- No paper on universally meager or perfectly meager sets that I opened states an additivity result (Bartoszynski 2000/2001, Bartoszynski-Shelah, Pol-Zakrzewski, Weiss-Zakrzewski, Korch-Weiss, Haberl-Szewczak-Zdomskyy). Nothing transfers from the category side.
- arXiv API (abstract search, newest first), zbMATH Open, and the MathOverflow/Math.SE API returned no item on additivity of UN, UM or PM other than Goto's paper. No arXiv paper after 2026-07 mentions "universally null" in its abstract except Goto and a choiceless paper by J. Z. Chen (irrelevant).

THE LEMMA AND THE CARDINAL g ARE KNOWN
- I confirmed from the PDF of Bartoszynski-Roslanowski-Shelah, "Adding one random real" (arXiv:math/9406229): Theorem 1.1 (Pawlikowski, Krawczyk), item 3, reads "cov(N) >= b and non(N) <= d" in V^B, and the proof line says (3) is due to Krawczyk. This settles the direction left open in Remark 4 of the note.
- The same paper defines non*(N): the least size of a family X of Borel functions such that for every null H in the plane and every non-null Borel B, some f in X has {x in B : (x,f(x)) not in H} non-null. Lemma 3.2: non*(N) = non(N) in V^B. Theorem 3.9: non*(N) < min{non(N), d} is consistent.
- Claim (proved here): g <= non*(N). Proof: let X witness non*(N) and let H be a null Borel set in the plane. Taking B the whole line gives f in X with {x : (x,f(x)) not in H} non-null, hence non-empty, so graph(f) is not inside H. So the union of the graphs lies in no null set. Whether g = non*(N) is unproved. So the note's g is, up to this inequality, the known invariant non*(N), and g < min{d, non(N)} is consistent by Theorem 3.9.

NEW CONSEQUENCE OF THE NOTE (conditional on the note's Theorem; I did not re-check that Theorem)
- Goldstern-Judah-Shelah, "Strong measure zero sets without Cohen reals" (arXiv:math/9306214), Theorem 3.4: a model of c = aleph_2 where SN = [R]^{<=aleph_1}, built by a countable support iteration that the proof states is omega^omega-bounding over L (so d = aleph_1).
- In that model: every set of size aleph_1 is null, so non(N) = c; Grzegorek gives a UN set of size c; the note gives add(UN) <= d = aleph_1. Also add(SN) = add(SN,N) = aleph_2 trivially. So add(UN) < add(SN) = add(SN,N) is consistent. Goto's paper does not state this separation (keyword search of flat.txt). The steps "non(N) = c" and "add(SN,N) = aleph_2" are my own one-line deductions.
- With c = aleph_2 the note also gives: add(UN) = aleph_2 forces non(N) = d = aleph_2 (if add(UN) = c then non(N) = c, so a UN set of size c exists and add(UN) <= d).

CANDIDATE MODELS FOR add(N) < add(UN) (untested, unproved)
- GJS Theorem 0.16/3.9: c = d = aleph_2 > b, Add(S) (unions of fewer than c strong measure zero sets are strong measure zero), no Cohen reals. Here add(N) = aleph_1 and non(N) = d = c, so the note does not rule it out.
- GJS attribute to Pawlikowski a finite support iteration giving Add(S) + c = aleph_2 + b = aleph_1. Its iterands cannot satisfy Goto's Theorem 5.18 hypothesis, since add(SN) is large there.
- Contrast: Goto, arXiv:2610.08549v2 (Oct 2026), gets b = d = aleph_1 < add(N^h) = c = aleph_2 for the Davies-Rogers Hausdorff null ideal with a proper omega^omega-bounding iteration. By the previous paragraph that method cannot give add(UN) = aleph_2.

findings.source: T. Goto, Forcing and cardinal invariants of universally null sets, arXiv:2607.12936v4 (v4 dated 9 Oct 2026; arXiv abs page shows no v5)
findings.exactStatement: Proposition 5.12: add(UN,N) = add(UN). Corollary 5.13: add(N) <= add(UN). Question 6.3: Is it consistent that add(N) < add(UN), or does ZFC prove add(N) = add(UN)? Theorem 5.18 concludes that the iteration forces add(SN,N) <= theta.
findings.relevance: Source of the question. It cites no earlier work on add(UN). Its reference list has 13 items; none is about additivity of UN. The question is still listed as open in the latest version.

findings.source: D. H. Fremlin, Measure Theory vol. 5, chapter 54, section 544 (file chap54.pdf, version dated 23.10.14/17.9.16), 544L Corollary
findings.exactStatement: 544L Corollary. Let X be a metrizable space. (a) If Un is the sigma-ideal of universally negligible subsets of X, then add Un >= add N_omega. (b) unions of fewer than add N_omega universally measurable sets are universally measurable.
findings.relevance: Earlier statement of add(N) <= add(UN), in greater generality (non-separable metrizable spaces). No upper bound on add Un is given. Chapters 43, 52, 53, 55 and Fremlin's problem list contain no other statement on add Un (text search for 'universally negligible').

findings.source: T. Bartoszynski, A. Roslanowski, S. Shelah, Adding one random real, arXiv:math/9406229v1
findings.exactStatement: Theorem 1.1 (Pawlikowski, Krawczyk). The following holds in V^B: ... 3. cov(N) >= b and non(N) <= d. Proof line: '(3) is due to Krawczyk (see [7] or [5])', where [5] = A. Krawczyk, Dominating reals add random reals, 1985, unpublished notes, and [7] = J. Pawlikowski, Why Solovay real produces Cohen real, JSL 51 (1986). Definition 3.1 defines cov*(N) and non*(N) via Borel functions and null subsets of the plane. Lemma 3.2: cov*(N) = cov(N)^{V^B} and non*(N) = non(N)^{V^B}. Theorem 3.9: it is consistent that cov*(N) > max{cov(N), b} and that non*(N) < min{non(N), d}.
findings.relevance: Confirms the direction of the inequality that Remark 4 of the note left unconfirmed. The note's Lemma (g <= d) is this known result in combinatorial form. The note's cardinal g satisfies g <= non*(N) (proved in my summary), so g is essentially a known invariant, and it can be strictly below min{d, non(N)}.

findings.source: M. Goldstern, H. Judah, S. Shelah, Strong measure zero sets without Cohen reals, arXiv:math/9306214v1 (J. Symbolic Logic 58 (1993), as cited by Haberl-Szewczak-Zdomskyy)
findings.exactStatement: 0.9: Add(S) means that for every kappa < c the union of kappa many strong measure zero sets is strong measure zero. 0.11 Theorem: If Unif(S) and d = c, then there exists a strong measure zero set of size c. Theorem 3.4: consistency of ZFC + c = aleph_2 + S = [R]^{<=aleph_1} + no real is Cohen over L + there is a generalized Sierpinski set; the proof says 'P_{omega_2} is omega^omega-bounding'. 0.16 / 3.9 Theorem: Con(ZFC + c = d = aleph_2 > b + Add(S) + no real is Cohen over L). Remark before 0.16: Pawlikowski [11] built a model of Add(S) + c = aleph_2 + b = aleph_1 by a finite support iteration of length omega_2.
findings.relevance: Closest classical analogue: additivity of the strong measure zero ideal can exceed add(N). Theorem 3.4 plus the note gives a model of add(UN) = aleph_1 < add(SN) = add(SN,N) = aleph_2 (conditional on the note). The 3.9 model and Pawlikowski's model are untested candidates for add(N) < add(UN). GJS's reference [11] is listed as J. Pawlikowski, Power of transitive bases of measure and category, Proc. AMS 93 (1985) 719-729; I did not open that paper.

findings.source: T. Goto, The additivity of a certain Hausdorff measure can differ from that of the Lebesgue measure, arXiv:2610.08549v2 (Oct 2026)
findings.exactStatement: Corollary 2: each of the following is consistent: aleph_1 = b = d < add(N^h_Omega) = c = aleph_2; aleph_1 = cof(N^h_Omega) < b = d = c = aleph_2. Corollary 3: add(N) < add(N^h_Omega) and cof(N^h_Omega) < cof(N) are each consistent. Model (1) is obtained by iterating a proper omega^omega-bounding forcing that adds an eventual localizing slalom.
findings.relevance: Same author, three months later, separates add(N) from the additivity of another null-type ideal. The paper does not mention universally null sets (text search). By the note, this omega^omega-bounding method cannot give add(UN) = aleph_2 = c.

findings.source: J. Brendle, P. Larson, Nonmeager universally null sets, unpublished note dated June 8, 2017
findings.exactStatement: Theorem 0.1. If min{d, non(Null)} = cof(Meager) then there exists a nonmeager universally null set of cardinality cof(Meager).
findings.relevance: Read in full (2 pages). It uses compact determination by dominating functions, as in tool 4 of context.md. It has no statement on additivity of UN.

findings.source: P. Larson, I. Neeman, S. Shelah, Universally measurable sets in generic extensions, arXiv:1003.2479 and the UCLA copy UM.pdf
findings.exactStatement: MA_kappa implies that the union of kappa many null sets is null for any Borel measure on a Polish space, hence unions of kappa many Borel sets are universally measurable. Theorem 2.8 (Grzegorek): if lambda is the least cardinality of a nonmeasurable set of reals, then there is a universally null set of cardinality lambda. A universally null set of cardinality lambda cannot be a union of fewer than lambda Borel sets.
findings.relevance: Only union-type statements in this paper. No additivity number for UN.

literature.summary:
Literature task D, finished 20:10 EST. Question 6.3 is not answered. The main finding is that the Mathias model is no longer a candidate, conditional on the note's Theorem in its g-form (Remark 1 of add-UN-note.md, which has had one AI review and which I re-derived here).

**Mathias model ruled out (conditional).** The note's invariant g is bounded by a known invariant. Bartoszynski-Roslanowski-Shelah (BRS) define non*(N), and g ≤ non*(N). Proof: if X witnesses non*(N) and the union of its graphs lay in a null H, then with B = R every f in X has {x : (x,f(x)) not in H} empty, a contradiction. BRS prove non*(N) = non(N) in the one-random-real extension, cov(M) ≤ non*(N) ≤ min{d, non(SN)}, and that non*(N) ≤ b implies non*(N) = cov(M). So if a UN set of size c exists, add(UN) ≤ min{d, non(SN)}. In the Mathias model non(N) = c, so Grzegorek gives a UN set of size c. Also non(SN) = aleph_1 there: one Mathias real makes every uncountable ground set non-SMZ, and the tail has the Laver property. Hence add(UN) = aleph_1 = add(N). The same holds in any model of the Borel Conjecture with a UN set of size c. I did not prove g = non*(N).

**Models.** All derivations below are mine from the fetched statements plus ZFC inequalities.
- Laver model: cov(N) = non(N) = cov(M) = aleph_1 and b = d = aleph_2 (fetched). So add(UN) ≤ non(N) = aleph_1. Out.
- Mathias model: cov(M) = cov(N) = add(N) = aleph_1 and b = d = s = non(M) = non(N) = c = aleph_2. Mathias forcing has the Laver property. No single fetched source lists all values or says "BC holds in the Mathias model"; I assembled them. No literature on UN sets in this model was found.
- Goldstern-Judah-Shelah (GJS) Theorems 0.14 and 0.15 (iteration of PT_H, plus random forcing for 0.15): SN = [R]^{≤aleph_1}, so d = aleph_1 < non(N) = c. The note's Theorem gives add(UN) = aleph_1, while add(SN) = add(SN,N) = aleph_2. Goto's bound add(SN,N) gives nothing here.
- GJS Theorem 0.16 (iteration of PT_H and rational perfect forcing): c = d = aleph_2 > b, Add(S), no Cohen reals. Then add(N) = cov(M) = b = aleph_1 and d = non(SN) = non(N) = add(SN) = add(SN,N) = aleph_2. Every known upper bound for add(UN) equals aleph_2. This is the one surviving candidate found; g is undetermined there.
- Bartoszynski-Shelah product of kappa copies of EE: non(SN) = c > d = aleph_1. Their Lemma 3.4 gives aleph_1 SN sets covering 2^omega, so add(UN) ≤ add(SN,N) = aleph_1 without the note.
- Countable support iteration of EE: d = aleph_1 and non(N) = aleph_2, so add(UN) = aleph_1 by the note. Bartoszynski-Judah section 7.4 itself was not fetched.

**Larson-Zapletal.** N_1 is a measured extension of N_0 (Definition 5.1) if (1) every countable subset of N_0 in N_1 is covered by a set countable in N_0, and (2) for a family F of Borel sets in N_0 and rational eps > 0, a measure in N_1 giving every i(B) mass ≥ eps yields a measure in N_0 giving every B mass ≥ eps. Proposition 5.2 controls UN sets: if N_0 picks for each measure mu a Borel B_mu of mass < 1, every point of N_1 misses some i(B_mu). Theorem 5.12: countable support iterations of iterable Sigma^1_1-polar forcings give measured extensions. Propositions 5.3 and 5.4: measured extensions are bounding and preserve outer measure. So a measured extension of a CH model has non(N) = aleph_1 and add(UN) = aleph_1. The technique cannot produce add(N) < add(UN), and it applies to none of the Mathias, Laver, EE, PT_H or Miller iterations.

**Other.** The Krawczyk inequality in the note's Remark 4 is confirmed from the PDF: after one random real, non(N) ≤ d. Statements in the findings are symbolic transcriptions of the fetched text, not verbatim quotes. Text extractions are in scratch/txt/ (may be cleared).

Definition 1.1: non*(N) = min{|X| : X a set of Borel maps R->R such that for every null H in the plane and every non-null Borel B some f in X has {x in B : (x,f(x)) not in H} non-null}; cov*(N) dually. Proposition 1.2: cov*(N) = cov(N)^{V^B} and non*(N) = non(N)^{V^B}, B the measure algebra adding one random real. Theorem 3.3: cov*(N) >= kappa* and non*(N) <= lambda*, where lambda* = inf_f b(R^exists_f). Lemma 3.5: lambda* = non(SN) (attributed to Miller) and kappa* >= non(SM). findings.exactStatement: Transcribed. Definition 3.1: a sigma-ideal I on Polish X generated by analytic sets is polar if some set M of Borel probability measures satisfies, for analytic A: A not in I iff some mu in M has mu(A) > 0 iff some mu in M has mu(A) = 1. It is Sigma^1_1-polar if M can be analytic, and iterable if the quotient P_I is proper in all forcing extensions. Examples of iterable Sigma^1_1-polar ideals: countable sets (Sacks), nu-null sets (random), countable product of Sacks, E_0-selectors, capacity-null sets, sets of extended uniqueness. Example 3.8: the ideal generated by compact subsets of Baire space is not polar. Definition 5.1: for transitive N_0 subset N_1 with the same ordinals, N_1 is a measured extension of N_0 if (1) every a in N_1 with a subset N_0 and countable in N_1 is covered by a set in N_0 countable there; (2) for rational eps > 0, Polish X in N_0 and a family F in N_0 of Borel subsets of X: if N_1 has a Borel probability measure mu_1 on i(X) with mu_1(i(B)) >= eps for all B in F, then N_0 has mu_0 with mu_0(B) >= eps for all B in F. Proposition 5.2: if N_1 is a measured extension of N_0 and in N_0 each Borel probability mu on X is assigned a Borel B_mu with mu(B_mu) < 1, then for every x in i(X) in N_1 there is mu with x not in i(B_mu). Proposition 5.3: measured extensions are bounding. Proposition 5.4: measured extensions preserve outer measure. Proposition 5.5: the relation is transitive. Theorem 5.6: in a measured extension there is a unique map from UM(X)^{N_0} to UM(i(X))^{N_1} commuting with the sigma-algebra operations and extending the interpretation of open sets. Theorem 5.12: for an iterable Sigma^1_1-polar ideal I and any ordinal alpha, the countable support iteration of P_I of length alpha gives a measured extension of the ground model.

findings.exactStatement: (a) Proved: g <= non*(N). If X witnesses non*(N) and the union of its graphs were inside a null H, take B = R; then every f in X has {x : (x,f(x)) not in H} empty, contradicting the defining property. (c) Mathias model: non(SN) = aleph_1 and non(N) = c, so add(UN) = aleph_1. More generally BC plus a UN set of size c gives add(UN) = aleph_1. (d) A model of add(N) < add(UN) with a UN set of size c needs add(N) < min{d, non(SN)}; for c = aleph_2 this means Unif(S), d = c and add(N) = aleph_1. I did not check this carefully and it does not cover Borel functions. (f) Proved from Larson-Zapletal Proposition 5.4: in a measured extension of a CH model the ground reals stay non-null, so non(N) = aleph_1 = add(UN).

attacks.approach: I worked with the reformulation of (‡): add(UN) ≤ κ as soon as there are κ Borel partial maps φ_ξ and a universally null set P such that one can pick points w_β in prescribed positive compact sets with φ_ξ(β)(w_β) = c_β for distinct c_β ∈ P. The new ingredient is a "marker + message" coding read along a function f ∈ ω^ω. For each (n,k) a private block of coordinates carries a long all-zero marker and the first n bits of a message; φ_f(w) is the limit of the messages found at the blocks (n, f(n)) whose marker is present. This is a limsup-type (not graph-type) coding, so "infinitely often" suffices where the earlier note needed domination. A fusion argument shows: for every positive compact K and every c there is a slalom S of a fixed width h such that every f that escapes S infinitely often has a point w ∈ K with φ_f(w) = c. The width bound is independent of the history of the fusion by a second-moment (Cauchy–Schwarz) count, so no split into the cases b and add*(N) is needed; the direction of the slalom characterisation of add(N) that is used is proved directly. No file in the folder was edited.
attacks.summary:
Proved: if there is a universally null set of cardinality cof(N), then add(UN) = add(N). This covers non(N) = cof(N) (so non(N) = c), every model with c ≤ ℵ_2 (Mathias, Laver, Miller, Sacks, all countable support iterations over CH), and supersedes the bound add(UN) ≤ d of add-UN-note.md.

Question 6.3 itself is not settled in ZFC. A model of add(N) < add(UN) must now satisfy add(N) < add(UN) ≤ non(N) < cof(N), have every universally null set of size < cof(N) (so b < cof(N)), and have c ≥ ℵ_3.

The proof has not been reviewed by anyone else. A quick web search found no prior statement of the result; this is not a full literature search. The remaining obstruction is a selector problem, stated in the obstacles.

claims.statement: Lemma 1 (non-localised family). Let h : ω → ω∖{0}. A slalom of width h is a map S from ω to finite subsets of ω with |S(n)| ≤ h(n); it localises f ∈ ω^ω if f(n) ∈ S(n) for all but finitely many n. There is F ⊆ ω^ω with |F| ≤ add(N) such that no slalom of width h localises every member of F.
claims.proof:
Let λ be the product measure on 2^ω. Put ε_n = 2^{-n}/h(n). Fix an enumeration (O_k)_{k∈ω} of the clopen subsets of 2^ω.

Step 1. Every null G ⊆ 2^ω is contained in limsup_n C_n for some clopen sets C_n with λ(C_n) ≤ ε_n. Proof: for each j pick an open O^j ⊇ G with λ(O^j) ≤ ε_j 2^{-j-1}, and write O^j as a disjoint union of cylinders [t^j_i], i < N_j ≤ ω. For fixed j choose 0 = i_0 < i_1 ≤ i_2 ≤ ... with i_r ≥ r and Σ_{i ≥ i_r} λ[t^j_i] ≤ ε_{j+r} 2^{-j-1} for r ≥ 1 (tails of a convergent series tend to 0). Let group r of j be {i : i_r ≤ i < i_{r+1}}; it is finite, and its cylinders have total measure ≤ ε_{j+r} 2^{-j-1} (for r = 0 this is the bound on λ(O^j)). Let C_n be the union of the cylinders in group n−j of j, over all j ≤ n. Then C_n is clopen and λ(C_n) ≤ ε_n Σ_j 2^{-j-1} ≤ ε_n. If x ∈ G then for each j, x lies in some [t^j_i], hence in C_n for some n ≥ j; so x ∈ C_n for infinitely many n.

Step 2. Let {G_ξ : ξ < add(N)} be null sets whose union is not null. By Step 1 choose f_ξ ∈ ω^ω with λ(O_{f_ξ(n)}) ≤ ε_n for all n and G_ξ ⊆ limsup_n O_{f_ξ(n)}. Let F = {f_ξ}. Suppose a slalom S of width h localises every f_ξ. Put D_n = ⋃{O_k : k ∈ S(n), λ(O_k) ≤ ε_n}. Then λ(D_n) ≤ h(n) ε_n = 2^{-n}, so G* = limsup_n D_n is null (Borel–Cantelli). Fix ξ and x ∈ G_ξ. For infinitely many n we have x ∈ O_{f_ξ(n)}, and for all large n we have f_ξ(n) ∈ S(n), hence O_{f_ξ(n)} ⊆ D_n. So x ∈ G*. Thus ⋃_ξ G_ξ ⊆ G* is null, a contradiction. ∎

claims.statement:
Lemma 2 (coding lemma). Put μ_n = 4^{n+1}, α_n = 2^{-μ_n}, ρ_n = 2^{-μ_n-n}, h(n) = 2^{3μ_n+n}. Fix pairwise disjoint finite sets B_{n,k} ⊆ ω ((n,k) ∈ ω×ω) with |B_{n,k}| = μ_n + n, enumerated increasingly as b_{n,k}(0) < ... < b_{n,k}(μ_n+n−1). For w ∈ 2^ω say that w has a marker at (n,k) if w(b_{n,k}(j)) = 0 for all j < μ_n, and let msg_{n,k}(w) ∈ 2^n be i ↦ w(b_{n,k}(μ_n+i)). For f ∈ ω^ω let D(w,f) = {n : w has a marker at (n,f(n))}. Let dom(φ_f) be the set of w such that D(w,f) is infinite and for every i the bits msg_{n,f(n)}(w)(i), n ∈ D(w,f), n > i, are eventually constant; φ_f(w)(i) is that constant. Then dom(φ_f) is Borel and φ_f : dom(φ_f) → 2^ω is Borel. 

Claim: for every compact K ⊆ 2^ω with λ(K) > 0 and every c ∈ 2^ω there is a slalom S of width h such that for every f ∈ ω^ω with f(n) ∉ S(n) for infinitely many n there is w ∈ K ∩ dom(φ_f) with φ_f(w) = c.
claims.proof:
Notation. A_{n,k} = {w : w has a marker at (n,k)}, R_{n,k} = A_{n,k} ∩ {w : msg_{n,k}(w) = c|n}, W_{n,k} = A_{n,k} ∖ R_{n,k}. These are clopen, λ(A_{n,k}) = α_n, λ(R_{n,k}) = ρ_n, λ(W_{n,k}) ≤ α_n, R_{n,k} ∩ W_{n,k} = ∅. Events that depend on disjoint sets of coordinates are independent. Put τ_n = Σ_{m>n} α_m (also for n = −1). Arithmetic: τ_{n−1} = τ_n + α_n; α_n ≤ τ_{n−1}; τ_n ≤ 2α_{n+1} = 2^{1−4μ_n} because μ_{m+1} ≥ μ_m + 1; hence (E) ρ_n τ_{n−1} ≥ ρ_n α_n = 2^{−2μ_n−n} ≥ 2^{2−4μ_n} ≥ 2τ_n, using 2μ_n ≥ n+2.

Definition of S. Choose n_0 ≥ 1 with 2τ_{n_0−1} ≤ λ(K). Put S(n) = ∅ for n < n_0. By recursion on n ≥ n_0 define, for every s ∈ ω^n, a closed set T^n(s) ⊆ K, and then S(n). Put T^{n_0}(s) = K. Given T^n(s') for all s' ∈ ω^n, let
 S(n) = {k : there is s' ∈ ω^n with λ(T^n(s') ∩ R_{n,k}) < (ρ_n/2) λ(T^n(s'))},
and for s = s'⌢k ∈ ω^{n+1} let T^{n+1}(s) = T^n(s') ∩ R_{n,k} if k ∉ S(n), and T^{n+1}(s) = T^n(s') ∖ W_{n,k} if k ∈ S(n). So T^n(s) = K ∩ E(s), where E(s) is a Boolean combination of events at blocks B_{m,s(m)}, m < n; E(s) depends only on coordinates in ⋃_{m<n,k} B_{m,k}.

Invariant: λ(T^n(s)) ≥ 2τ_{n−1} for all n ≥ n_0 and s ∈ ω^n. For n = n_0 this is the choice of n_0. Step: if k ∈ S(n), then λ(T^{n+1}(s)) ≥ 2τ_{n−1} − α_n = 2τ_n + α_n ≥ 2τ_n. If k ∉ S(n), then by definition of S(n), λ(T^{n+1}(s)) ≥ (ρ_n/2) λ(T^n(s')) ≥ ρ_n τ_{n−1} ≥ 2τ_n by (E).

Width: |S(n)| ≤ h(n). Fix n ≥ n_0, put ρ = ρ_n, θ = 2τ_{n−1}. Let k_1,...,k_N be distinct elements of S(n) with witnesses s_1,...,s_N; put E_j = E(s_j), T_j = K ∩ E_j, R_j = R_{n,k_j}. Then λ(T_j) ≥ θ and λ(T_j ∩ R_j) < (ρ/2)λ(T_j). Let Ξ = Σ_j 1_{E_j}·(ρ − 1_{R_j}). Then ∫_K Ξ dλ = Σ_j (ρ λ(T_j) − λ(T_j ∩ R_j)) > Σ_j (ρ/2) λ(T_j) ≥ Nρθ/2. The sets E_j depend only on coordinates in stage-m blocks, m < n; R_j depends only on B_{n,k_j}; the blocks B_{n,k_j} are pairwise disjoint and disjoint from all earlier blocks. Hence for j ≠ j' the functions 1_{E_j}1_{E_j'}, ρ − 1_{R_j}, ρ − 1_{R_j'} are independent and the last two have mean 0, so the cross terms of ∫Ξ² vanish and ∫Ξ² = Σ_j λ(E_j) ρ(1−ρ) ≤ Nρ. By Cauchy–Schwarz, ∫_K Ξ ≤ (∫Ξ²)^{1/2} ≤ (Nρ)^{1/2}. So Nρθ/2 < (Nρ)^{1/2}, i.e. N < 4/(ρθ²) = 1/(ρ_n τ_{n−1}²) ≤ 1/(ρ_n α_n²) = 2^{3μ_n+n} = h(n). So S(n) is finite with at most h(n) elements.

The point w. Let f satisfy f(n) ∉ S(n) for infinitely many n. For n ≥ n_0 put Q_n = T^n(f|n) ∖ ⋃_{m≥n} W_{m,f(m)}. Q_n is closed, and λ(Q_n) ≥ 2τ_{n−1} − Σ_{m≥n} α_m = τ_{n−1} > 0. Since R_{n,k} ∩ W_{n,k} = ∅, in both cases T^{n+1}(f|(n+1)) ⊆ T^n(f|n) ∖ W_{n,f(n)}, so Q_{n+1} ⊆ Q_n. By compactness pick w ∈ ⋂_{n≥n_0} Q_n. Then w ∈ K; w ∉ W_{m,f(m)} for all m ≥ n_0; and w ∈ R_{n,f(n)} for every n ≥ n_0 with f(n) ∉ S(n) (because w ∈ T^{n+1}(f|(n+1))). So D(w,f) is infinite. If n ∈ D(w,f) and n ≥ n_0, then w ∈ A_{n,f(n)} ∖ W_{n,f(n)} = R_{n,f(n)}, so msg_{n,f(n)}(w) = c|n. Hence for each i, every n ∈ D(w,f) with n > max(i,n_0) gives bit c(i). So w ∈ dom(φ_f) and φ_f(w) = c.

Borelness: dom(φ_f) is defined by countable quantifiers over clopen conditions, and each coordinate of φ_f is Borel on it. ∎

claims.statement: Lemma 3 (transfer of universal nullness). Let Δ ⊆ 2^ω be Borel, φ : Δ → 2^ω Borel, P ⊆ 2^ω universally null, and X ⊆ Δ such that φ[X] ⊆ P and φ is injective on X. Then X is universally null.
claims.proof: Let μ be an atomless finite Borel measure on 2^ω. Define the finite Borel measure ν(B) = μ(Δ ∩ φ^{-1}[B]). Let At = {c : ν({c}) > 0}; it is countable. ν_0(B) = ν(B ∖ At) is a finite Borel measure with no point masses, hence atomless. Since P is universally null there is a Borel B ⊇ P with ν_0(B) = 0, that is μ(Δ ∩ φ^{-1}[B ∖ At]) = 0. Now X ⊆ (Δ ∩ φ^{-1}[B ∖ At]) ∪ (X ∩ φ^{-1}[At]). The first set is μ-null. The second is countable because φ is injective on X and At is countable; it is μ-null because μ is atomless. So μ*(X) = 0. ∎

claims.statement: Theorem. If there is a universally null set of cardinality cof(N), then add(UN) = add(N).
claims.proof:
add(N) ≤ add(UN) is Goto's Corollary 5.13 (in flat.txt). For the other inequality let h and (φ_f) be as in Lemma 2 and let F be given by Lemma 1 for this h; |F| ≤ add(N).

Let {G_β : β < cof(N)} be a cofinal family of null sets; we may take each G_β to be a G_δ. Its complement is an F_σ of measure 1, so it contains a compact K_β with λ(K_β) > 0. Any set X that meets every K_β is not null: if X were null, X ⊆ G_β for some β, but X ∩ K_β ≠ ∅ and K_β ∩ G_β = ∅.

Let P be universally null with |P| = cof(N) (take a subset of the given set) and let {c_β : β < cof(N)} list P without repetition. For each β let S_β be the slalom of width h given by Lemma 2 for (K_β, c_β). F is not localised by S_β, so there is f_β ∈ F with f_β(n) ∉ S_β(n) for infinitely many n. Lemma 2 gives w_β ∈ K_β ∩ dom(φ_{f_β}) with φ_{f_β}(w_β) = c_β.

For f ∈ F put X_f = {w_β : f_β = f}. Then φ_f[X_f] ⊆ P, and φ_f is injective on X_f: if w_β = w_β' with f_β = f_β' = f then c_β = φ_f(w_β) = c_β'. By Lemma 3, X_f is universally null. The union of the X_f, f ∈ F, is {w_β : β < cof(N)}; it meets every K_β, so it is not Lebesgue null, hence not universally null. So |F| ≤ add(N) universally null sets have a union that is not universally null, and add(UN) ≤ add(N). ∎

claims.statement: Corollaries. (a) If non(N) = cof(N), in particular if non(N) = c, then add(UN) = add(N). (b) If c ≤ ℵ_2 then add(UN) = add(N). (c) If add(N) < add(UN), then every universally null set has cardinality < cof(N), b < cof(N), add(N) < add(UN) ≤ non(N) < cof(N), and c ≥ ℵ_3.
claims.proof:
Facts quoted from Goto's paper (flat.txt; the original papers of Grzegorek and Recław were not checked): there is a universally null set of size non(N) (Grzegorek); there is one of size b (Recław); add(N) ≤ add(UN) ≤ non(UN) = non(N). Also non(N) ≤ cof(N) ≤ c (standard).

(a) Grzegorek's set has size non(N) = cof(N); apply the Theorem. If non(N) = c then cof(N) = c.

(c) Assume add(N) < add(UN). By the Theorem there is no universally null set of size cof(N); since subsets of universally null sets are universally null, every universally null set has size < cof(N). By Grzegorek and Recław, non(N) < cof(N) and b < cof(N). So ℵ_1 ≤ add(N) < add(UN) ≤ non(N) < cof(N) ≤ c, which forces c ≥ ℵ_3.

(b) Immediate from (c): if c ≤ ℵ_2 the chain in (c) is impossible, so add(N) = add(UN). ∎

claims.statement: Proposition 6 (self-coding criterion; reduces the remaining case to a selector problem). Let κ be a cardinal, 𝒩 ⊆ 2^ω × 2^ω a Borel set all of whose sections 𝒩_c = {y : (c,y) ∈ 𝒩} are Lebesgue null, and ψ_ξ (ξ < κ) Borel maps with Borel domains dom(ψ_ξ) ⊆ 2^ω into 2^ω. Let θ be a limit ordinal and Y = {y_γ : γ < θ} ⊆ 2^ω a set that is not Lebesgue null such that every Y_γ = {y_δ : δ < γ} has cardinality < non(N), and for every γ there is ξ(γ) < κ with y_γ ∈ dom(ψ_ξ(γ)) and Y_γ ⊆ 𝒩_{ψ_ξ(γ)(y_γ)}. Then add(UN) ≤ κ.
claims.proof: For ξ < κ put Y^ξ = {y_γ : ξ(γ) = ξ}. The union of the Y^ξ is Y, which is not null, hence not universally null. It remains to show each Y^ξ is universally null. Fix ξ and an atomless finite Borel measure μ on 2^ω. Let R = {(y,w) : w ∈ dom(ψ_ξ) and (ψ_ξ(w), y) ∈ 𝒩}; R is Borel, and for each w the set {y : (y,w) ∈ R} is empty or a section of 𝒩, hence Lebesgue null. By Fubini (λ×μ)(R) = 0, so the set B = {y : μ({w : (y,w) ∈ R}) > 0} is Lebesgue null. Y is not null, so there is γ_0 with y_{γ_0} ∉ B. If γ > γ_0 and ξ(γ) = ξ, then y_{γ_0} ∈ Y_γ ⊆ 𝒩_{ψ_ξ(y_γ)}, so (y_{γ_0}, y_γ) ∈ R. Hence Y^ξ ⊆ {w : (y_{γ_0}, w) ∈ R} ∪ Y_{γ_0+1}. The first set is μ-null. The second has cardinality < non(N) = non(UN) (Goto), so it is universally null. So μ*(Y^ξ) = 0. ∎

obstacles: Remaining case: non(N) < cof(N) and every universally null set has size < cof(N). The proof of the Theorem picks one point per member of a cofinal family of positive compact sets, so it needs cof(N) distinct codes. Any decomposition X = ⋃_{f∈F} X_f into universally null pieces has |X| at most the supremum of sizes of universally null sets, so in this case X must be a non-null set of size < cof(N): a small set has to defeat cof(N) many null sets, which cannot be arranged by a recursion over the null sets.

Sharpest precise statement left open (unproved). With F and φ_f from Lemmas 1–2 and a Borel 𝒩 with null sections that is universal for null sets, put L(A) = {w : there is f ∈ F with A ⊆ 𝒩_{φ_f(w)}}. By Lemma 2, L(A) meets every positive compact set whenever A is null (not written out as a claim; it needs only that A lies in some section of 𝒩). Statement (O): there is a non-null Y = {y_γ : γ < non(N)} with y_γ ∈ L({y_δ : δ < γ}) for all γ. By Proposition 6, (O) implies add(UN) = add(N) in ZFC. Equivalently one needs a non-null selector of the decreasing sequence of full-outer-measure sets L(Y_γ), where the sequence depends on the selector. A model of add(N) < add(UN) must make every such self-coded Y null.

Routes tried for (O) that fail. (1) Moving a given non-null Z into L(·) by a countable group or finitely many non-singular Borel maps: impossible, since all codable points lie in ⋃_f dom(φ_f), a union of add(N) null sets. (2) Rewriting the messages of points of a non-null Z ⊆ ⋃_f dom(φ_f): non-nullness is not preserved in general; a sufficient condition is that every null set misses a whole rewriting class C_{f,z} for some z ∈ Z, which is a uniformity statement for a larger ideal than N. (3) Product and Fubini tricks (graphs over a non-null set, two message channels, products of universally null sets): each reduces to the same selector problem one dimension lower. (4) Elementary chains of submodels of size non(N): the resulting set meets every positive compact set coded in the model, but that gives non-nullness only when the model's null sets are cofinal, i.e. non(N) = cof(N). (5) Demanding that all (or measure-positively many) message rewritings stay in K: a second-moment sketch suggests this works with a fixed width, but the Fubini obstacle then forbids taking the code from a universally null set.

Constraints on a model of add(N) < add(UN), from the Theorem and Goto's results: add(N) < add(UN) ≤ non(N) < cof(N); c ≥ ℵ_3; every universally null set has size < cof(N), so b < cof(N); not a finite support iteration of the kind covered by Goto's Theorem 5.18. All countable support iterations over CH are excluded, including the Mathias model.

Citations not checked: the slalom characterisation of add(N) (Bartoszyński) and Pawlikowski's add(N) = min(b, add*(N)) were recalled from memory and are not used; Lemma 1 proves the one direction needed. Grzegorek's and Recław's theorems are used only as quoted in Goto's paper.

errors: Claim 4 (Theorem), step 'φ_f is injective on X_f: if w_β = w_β' with f_β = f_β' = f then c_β = φ_f(w_β) = c_β''. This proves the converse implication (equal points have equal images, which holds for any function). It does not prove injectivity. Repair, one line: if w_β, w_β' ∈ X_f and φ_f(w_β) = φ_f(w_β'), then c_β = c_β', so β = β' because the enumeration of P has no repetition, so w_β = w_β'. With this the hypothesis of Lemma 3 holds and the Theorem stands. This is the only step I found that does not prove what it says.

Summary wording (not a proof step): 'all countable support iterations over CH' is too broad. Corollary (b) needs c ≤ ℵ_2 in the extension. That holds for length-ω_2 countable support iterations of proper posets of size ≤ ℵ_1 over CH, not for every countable support iteration. State (b) only as 'c ≤ ℵ_2'.
referees.notes:
Verdict in short: every statement (Claims 1-6) is correct as far as I can check. One step in Claim 4 is written in the wrong direction and needs the one-line repair above. I found no other gap. I started from the assumption that the proof was wrong and could not break it.

What I checked, claim by claim.

Claim 1 (Lemma 1). Correct. Step 1: groups are finite, λ(C_n) ≤ Σ_{j≤n} ε_n 2^{-j-1} ≤ ε_n, and each x ∈ G lies in some C_n with n ≥ j for every j. Step 2: λ(D_n) ≤ h(n)ε_n = 2^{-n}, Borel-Cantelli, and G_ξ ⊆ limsup D_n. The direction is the one needed: a non-localised family of size ≤ add(N). The statement also holds for bounded h, so there is no hidden growth hypothesis.

Claim 2 (Lemma 2). Correct. I rechecked:
- Arithmetic: μ_{n+1} = 4μ_n, τ_n ≤ 2α_{n+1} = 2^{1-4μ_n}, (E) needs 2μ_n ≥ n+2, and 1/(ρ_n α_n²) = 2^{3μ_n+n} (also checked by script for n ≤ 5).
- Invariant λ(T^n(s)) ≥ 2τ_{n-1} in both cases.
- Width bound. ∫_K Ξ > Nρθ/2 uses only the definition of S(n) and the invariant. The cross terms of ∫Ξ² vanish because E_j, E_j' use only blocks of stages < n and R_j, R_j' use the distinct blocks B_{n,k_j}, B_{n,k_j'}; all blocks are pairwise disjoint. K enters only through Cauchy-Schwarz with ‖1_K‖_2 ≤ 1, so no independence of K is needed. This gives N < 1/(ρ_n τ_{n-1}²) ≤ h(n) for all witnesses s_j at once. There is no measurability problem: every set is clopen or closed.
- Fusion: Q_{n+1} ⊆ Q_n because R ∩ W = ∅; λ(Q_n) ≥ τ_{n-1} > 0; a point of ⋂Q_n has the right message at every marker from n_0 on, and has markers at the infinitely many n with f(n) ∉ S(n).
- Sanity test: each fibre φ_f^{-1}{c} is null (Σρ_n < ∞), so the lemma yields add(N) Borel null sets with full outer measure union. That is consistent, and matches the known Tukey direction of the slalom characterisation of add(N).

Claim 3 (Lemma 3). Correct. ν_0 has no point masses, hence is atomless; the cover X ⊆ φ^{-1}[B∖At] ∪ (X ∩ φ^{-1}[At]) is right; the second set is countable by injectivity.

Claim 4 (Theorem). Statement correct after the repair above. The K_β argument, the use of Lemma 1 with the h of Lemma 2 (|S(n)| < h(n)), and 'not Lebesgue null hence not UN' are all right. add(N) ≤ add(UN) is Corollary 5.13 in flat.txt (confirmed).

Claim 5 (Corollaries). Correct. Grzegorek (UN set of size non(N)), Recław (size b) and non(UN) = non(N) (Proposition 5.4) are quoted in flat.txt as stated; the original papers were not checked, as the author says. b < cof(N) follows directly from Recław's set, without b ≤ cof(N). The chain ℵ_1 ≤ add(N) < add(UN) ≤ non(N) < cof(N) ≤ c gives c ≥ ℵ_3.

Claim 6 (Proposition 6). Correct. R is Borel, every w-section is empty or a section of 𝒩, Fubini gives a λ-null Borel set B, and Y^ξ ⊆ R_{y_{γ_0}} ∪ Y_{γ_0+1} with |Y_{γ_0+1}| < non(N) = non(UN). θ limit is used for γ_0+1 < θ. The Fubini step is applied to a Borel set and a Borel measure, so there is no hidden non-measurability.

Tests against standard models. No conflict found.
- Cohen, Hechler, and the model of Corollary 5.19: non(N) = cof(N) = c and add(N) = ℵ_1; the Theorem gives add(UN) = ℵ_1, as Goto's Theorem 5.18 does.
- MA: all invariants equal c.
- Sacks, Laver, Miller, random: non(N) = ℵ_1, so the result is trivial there.
- Mathias: non(N) = c = ℵ_2 (from h ≤ s ≤ non(N), stated from memory, not fetched) and add(N) = ℵ_1, so the Theorem gives the new value add(UN) = ℵ_1. Nothing in context.md or flat.txt contradicts this.
- The claim that the Theorem supersedes add(UN) ≤ d is right: a UN set of size c contains one of size cof(N), and add(N) ≤ d.

Literature. Two web searches found no earlier statement of the Theorem and nothing that contradicts it. The only direct hit on add(UN) was Goto's paper. This is not a full literature search. Question 6.3 remains open in ZFC; the author's 'partial-result' status is accurate.

referees.notes:
I found no mathematical error in any of the six claims. The two entries under errors are wording fixes, not gaps. Finished 20:23 EST, before the 21:40 deadline. No file in the folder was edited.

**Claim 1 (Lemma 1): correct.**
- Step 1: the groups are finite, and lambda(C_n) <= eps_n * sum_j 2^{-j-1} <= eps_n. Each x in G lies in some C_n with n >= j for every j, so in infinitely many C_n.
- Step 2: lambda(D_n) <= h(n) eps_n = 2^{-n}, so Borel–Cantelli applies. 'Infinitely often in O_{f(n)}' plus 'eventually f(n) in S(n)' gives x in limsup D_n.
- The direction is right: a non-localised family of size <= add(N) exists for any h >= 1. No Fubini is used.

**Claim 2 (Lemma 2): correct. I rechecked every computation.**
- Arithmetic: alpha_{n+1} = 2^{-4 mu_n}, tau_n <= 2 alpha_{n+1}, and (E) reduces to 2 mu_n >= n+2.
- Invariant: both cases give lambda(T^{n+1}) >= 2 tau_n.
- Width: E_j depends only on blocks of stages below n. R_j and R_j' sit on two further disjoint blocks. So 1_{E_j}1_{E_j'}, rho - 1_{R_j}, rho - 1_{R_j'} are independent and the last two have mean 0. The cross terms vanish and the integral of Xi^2 is at most N rho.
- K enters only through Cauchy–Schwarz with 1_K, so no independence of K is needed. This gives N < 1/(rho_n tau_{n-1}^2) <= h(n), uniformly over the infinitely many histories s'.
- The recursion is not circular. The invariant at stage n is proved before S(n) is bounded and does not need S(n) finite.
- Fusion: Q_n is closed, decreasing, of measure >= tau_{n-1} > 0. A point w in the intersection avoids W_{m,f(m)} for all m >= n_0 and lies in R_{n,f(n)} whenever f(n) is not in S(n). So phi_f(w) = c.
- Borelness of dom(phi_f) and phi_f is clear.

**Claim 3 (Lemma 3): correct.** The pushforward nu is a finite Borel measure. Removing its countably many point masses gives a measure with no point masses, which is atomless on a Polish space. The exceptional part of X is countable by injectivity.

**Claim 4 (Theorem): correct, with the wording fix above.**
- Lemma 1 gives f_beta in F escaping S_beta infinitely often, which is exactly the hypothesis of Lemma 2.
- X_f is a subset of dom(phi_f), which is Borel, so Lemma 3 applies.
- {w_beta} meets every K_beta, so it is not Lebesgue null and hence not universally null.
- The recursion has length cof(N) and uses no cardinal arithmetic.

**Claim 5 (Corollaries): correct.** I confirmed the quoted facts in flat.txt:
- Corollary 5.13: add(N) <= add(UN).
- Proposition 5.4: non(UN) = non(N).
- Corollary 5.6(2),(3): universally null sets of size b (via Recław) and non(N) (via Grzegorek).

The chain aleph_1 <= add(N) < add(UN) <= non(N) < cof(N) <= c does force c >= aleph_3. Grzegorek's and Recław's original papers were not checked.

**Claim 6 (Proposition 6): correct.**
- R is Borel and every section over w is empty or a section of the null-section set, so Fubini applies to a Borel set. No non-measurable set enters.
- B is Borel and null, so some y_{gamma_0} lies outside it.
- Y_{gamma_0+1} is an initial segment because theta is a limit, so it has size < non(N) = non(UN).
- Repetitions in the enumeration do no harm.

**Tests against standard models: no conflict.**
- Cohen and Hechler: add(UN) = aleph_1 = add(N), matching Goto's Theorem 5.18. In Hechler, b = cof(N) gives the hypothesis.
- Random, Laver, Miller: non(N) = aleph_1, so the conclusion is trivial.
- Sacks: cof(N) = aleph_1, consistent with all universally null sets having size <= aleph_1.
- PT_{f,g}: the hypothesis fails if cof(N) = aleph_2 there, which I recalled from memory and did not check; if cof(N) = aleph_1 the conclusion is trivial.
- MA: add(N) = c.
- Mathias: the Theorem gives the new value add(UN) = aleph_1. I know of no lower bound on add(UN) (for example by h or p) that would contradict this. Goto's own MA(sigma-centered) models already have p = c with add(UN) = aleph_1.

**Consistency with context.md.**
- The scheme uses exactly add(N) Borel maps, so it respects the obstruction that fewer than add(N) pieces are killed by Fubini.
- Lemma 2 together with Lemma 1 re-derives both directions of the slalom characterisation of add(N). This is an internal consistency check.

**Literature.** Two web searches and a fetch of the arXiv record found no prior statement of the Theorem. The record (arxiv.org/abs/2607.12936) shows v4 of 9 Oct 2026 as the latest version, and its abstract does not mention the result. This is not a full literature search.

**Status.** The result remains partial. Question 6.3 is not settled in ZFC, as the author states. No human expert has checked the proof.

attacks.summary: Question 6.3 is NOT answered and add(UN) in the Mathias model is NOT decided. Proved (ZFC, self-contained): (1) a Reclaw-type lemma; (2) Theorem A: if F is a family of Borel maps 2^omega -> omega^omega such that for every S of size < c and every positive compact K some x in K and f in F have f(x) strictly eventually dominating S, then there are |F| universally null sets with non-null union, so add(UN) <= |F| (the hypothesis forces b = c, which holds in the Mathias model); (3) explicit decoders f_C (Hamming distance to a closed set C) with f_C(r + chi_a)(n) > a(n-1) when r in C and r + chi_a is not in C + fin; (4) every positive compact K contains r + 2^B for a positive-measure set of r whenever B is sparse relative to K; (5) Theorem B: under b = c, a 'no local cube' condition on a family of closed sets C gives add(UN) <= |C|; (6) a thin-tree lemma giving cube-freeness outside a thin hitting set W. Consequence (conditional on standard facts about the Mathias model, not re-proved): add(UN) = aleph_1 there as soon as, for every positive compact K, one can choose the sparse set B, a point r with r + 2^B inside K, and a ground-model (or V[G_alpha]) tree T through r whose hitting set W misses infinitely many points of B. I could not prove or refute this last decoupling statement; the obstacles are listed. Literature: a web search found no result on add(UN) in the Mathias or Laver model (Goto's Question 6.1 asks for cov(UN) there); Reclaw's theorem was confirmed as reference [9] of Goto's paper (I. Reclaw, On a construction of universally null sets, Real Anal. Exchange 27(1), 321-324; https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.rae/1212763971), and an independent proof is given below. Sources: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.12936 , https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.rae/1212763971 .

claims.statement: Lemma R (Reclaw-type). Let R be a Borel subset of 2^omega x 2^omega and Z a subset of 2^omega such that R restricted to Z x Z is a strict well-ordering of Z. Then Z is universally null.
claims.proof: Let mu be an atomless finite Borel measure on 2^omega and suppose mu*(Z) > 0. Enumerate Z in R-increasing order as {z_b : b < theta} and put Z_a = {z_b : b < a}. Let a0 <= theta be least with mu*(Z_{a0}) > 0. a0 is a limit ordinal: if a0 = a+1 then mu*(Z_{a0}) <= mu*(Z_a) + mu({z_a}) = 0 since mu is atomless. Put W = Z_{a0}. So mu*(Z_{b+1}) = 0 for every b < a0. Choose a Borel H containing W with mu(H) = mu*(W) > 0. Hull property: for every Borel E, mu(E cap H) = mu*(E cap W). (>= is clear. If mu*(E cap W) < mu(E cap H), pick Borel E' containing E cap W with mu(E') < mu(E cap H); then W is contained in (H minus E) union (E' cap E cap H), which has measure < mu(H), contradicting mu*(W) = mu(H).) Let R' = R cap (H x H), a Borel set. For y = z_b in W the Borel set {x in H : x R y} meets W in Z_b, so by the hull property its measure is mu*(Z_b) = 0. The set Y0 = {y in H : mu({x in H : x R y}) = 0} is Borel (measures of sections of a Borel set form a Borel function) and contains W, so H minus Y0 is a Borel set disjoint from W and has measure mu*(empty) = 0. By Fubini, (mu x mu)(R') = integral over H of mu({x in H : x R y}) dmu(y) = 0. For x = z_b in W the Borel set {y in H : x R y} meets W in W minus Z_{b+1}, whose outer measure is at least mu*(W) - mu*(Z_{b+1}) = mu(H); so its measure is mu(H). The Borel set X0 = {x in H : mu({y in H : x R y}) = mu(H)} contains W, so mu(H minus X0) = 0 and by Fubini (mu x mu)(R') = mu(H)^2 > 0. Contradiction. Hence mu*(Z) = 0.

claims.statement: Theorem A (ZFC). For s, u in omega^omega write s <* u if s(n) < u(n) for all but finitely many n. Let F be a family of Borel functions f : 2^omega -> omega^omega. Assume (H): for every S subset of omega^omega with |S| < c and every compact K subset of 2^omega with lambda(K) > 0 there are x in K and f in F with s <* f(x) for all s in S. Then there are universally null sets X_f (f in F) whose union is not Lebesgue null. Hence add(UN) <= |F|. (Hypothesis (H) implies b = c.)
claims.proof: List the compact sets of positive measure as {K_b : b < c}. By recursion on b < c choose x_b in K_b and f_b in F such that u_d <* u_b for all d < b, where u_b := f_b(x_b); this is (H) applied to S = {u_d : d < b} and K = K_b. For f in F put I_f = {b : f_b = f}, X_f = {x_b : b in I_f}, and R_f = {(x, x') : f(x) <* f(x')}. R_f is Borel, being the preimage of the Borel set {(u,v) : exists k forall n >= k u(n) < v(n)} under the Borel map (x,x') -> (f(x), f(x')). If d < b are in I_f then f(x_d) = u_d <* u_b = f(x_b), so (x_d, x_b) in R_f, and (x_b, x_d) is not in R_f because u <* v and v <* u cannot both hold. In particular x_d is different from x_b (otherwise u_d = u_b, but u <* u is false). So b -> x_b is injective on I_f and R_f restricted to X_f x X_f equals {(x_d, x_b) : d < b, both in I_f}, a strict well-ordering of X_f. By Lemma R each X_f is universally null. The union of the X_f is {x_b : b < c}, which meets every compact set of positive measure; a null set is contained in a null G_delta set whose complement contains a compact set of positive measure, so the union is not null, hence not universally null (lambda is an atomless finite Borel measure). Therefore |F| universally null sets have a union outside UN, i.e. add(UN) <= |F|. Finally (H) says in particular that every S of size < c has a <*-upper bound, so b = c.

claims.statement: Lemma D (Hamming decoder). Notation: + is coordinatewise addition mod 2 on 2^omega, chi_a is the characteristic function of a subset a of omega, fin = {chi_e : e finite}. For a nonempty closed C subset of 2^omega, x in 2^omega and N in omega let Delta_C(x,N) = min over c in C of |{i < N : x(i) != c(i)}|. Define f_C(x)(n) = the least N with Delta_C(x,N) >= n if such N exists, and 0 otherwise. Then f_C : 2^omega -> omega^omega is Borel, and: (a) if x is not in C + fin then for every n some N has Delta_C(x,N) >= n; (b) if x = r + chi_a with r in C, a an infinite subset of omega with increasing enumeration a(0) < a(1) < ..., and x is not in C + fin, then f_C(x)(n) > a(n-1) for every n >= 1.
claims.proof: Borel: for fixed n, N the set {x : Delta_C(x,N) >= n} depends only on x|N, so it is clopen; hence {x : f_C(x)(n) = N} is a Boolean combination of open sets. (a) Fix n and suppose Delta_C(x,N) < n for all N. Choose c_N in C with |{i < N : x(i) != c_N(i)}| < n. By compactness of C a subsequence of (c_N) converges to some c in C. For each M there is N >= M in the subsequence with c|M = c_N|M, so |{i < M : x(i) != c(i)}| <= |{i < N : x(i) != c_N(i)}| < n. Thus x and c differ in fewer than n places, so x is in C + fin. (b) Since r in C, Delta_C(x,N) <= |{i < N : x(i) != r(i)}| = |a cap N|. If N <= a(n-1) then a cap N is contained in {a(0),...,a(n-2)}, so Delta_C(x,N) <= n-1 < n. By (a) some N has Delta_C(x,N) >= n, and the least such N is > a(n-1).

claims.statement: Lemma E (cubes inside positive compact sets). Let K subset of 2^omega be compact with lambda(K) > 0. There is a strictly increasing sequence M_0 < M_1 < ... such that for every B subset of omega with B cap M_1 empty and |B cap M_{k+1}| <= k for all k >= 1, the set K_B = {r : r + chi_b in K for every b subset of B} is compact and has positive measure. Consequently, for every h in omega^omega there is an infinite such B whose increasing enumeration satisfies B(n) >= h(n) for all n (take B(n) >= max(h(n), M_{n+2})).
claims.proof: K_B is the intersection of the closed sets K + chi_b, so it is closed. Let O = 2^omega minus K. By the Lebesgue density theorem choose M_0 and s_0 in 2^{M_0} with lambda(O cap [s_0]) <= (1/4) 2^{-M_0}. For M >= M_0 let O^(M) be the union of the cylinders [t], t in 2^M extending s_0, with [t] subset of O. These sets increase with M and their union is O cap [s_0] because O is open. Put delta(M) = lambda(O cap [s_0]) - lambda(O^(M)); it decreases to 0 and delta(M_0) <= (1/4)2^{-M_0}. Note O^(M_0) is empty since [s_0] is not contained in O. Choose M_0 < M_1 < ... with delta(M_k) <= 8^{-k} 2^{-M_0} for k >= 1. Let B be as stated and r in [s_0] minus K_B. Pick b subset of B with r + chi_b in O. Since B cap M_0 is empty, r + chi_b in [s_0]. Let j be least with r + chi_b in O^(M_j); j >= 1. Put t = (r + chi_b)|M_j. Then [t] is one of the cylinders forming O^(M_j), and [t] is disjoint from O^(M_{j-1}) (the latter is a union of cylinders of length M_{j-1} <= M_j, so [t] is inside it or disjoint from it, and r + chi_b is not in it). Also r in [t + chi_e|M_j] with e = b cap M_j, a subset of B cap M_j, which has at most j-1 elements (for j = 1 because B cap M_1 is empty, for j >= 2 by the hypothesis with k = j-1). Let W_j be the set of t in 2^{M_j} with [t] subset of O^(M_j) minus O^(M_{j-1}); then |W_j| 2^{-M_j} <= delta(M_{j-1}). Hence [s_0] minus K_B is covered by the cylinders [t + chi_e|M_j], j >= 1, t in W_j, e subset of B cap M_j, of total measure at most sum_{j>=1} 2^{j-1} delta(M_{j-1}) = delta(M_0) + sum_{k>=1} 2^k delta(M_k) <= 2^{-M_0}(1/4 + sum_{k>=1} 4^{-k}) = (7/12) 2^{-M_0}. So lambda(K_B cap [s_0]) >= (5/12) 2^{-M_0} > 0. For the last sentence: if B(n) >= M_{n+2} then B cap M_1 is empty and, for k >= 1, B cap M_{k+1} is contained in {B(n) : n+2 <= k}, which has at most k-1 elements.

claims.statement: Theorem B (ZFC). Assume b = c. Let CC be a family of nonempty closed subsets of 2^omega. Assume (D): for every compact K of positive measure and every h in omega^omega there are an infinite B subset of omega, a point r in 2^omega and C in CC such that (i) B(n) >= h(n) for all n (increasing enumeration of B); (ii) r + chi_b in K for every b subset of B; (iii) r in C; (iv) there are no finite e subset of omega and finite F subset of B with r + chi_e + chi_b in C for all b subset of B minus F. Then add(UN) <= |CC|. (By Lemma E, (i) and (ii) can always be met, with a positive-measure set of admissible r; the content of (D) is (iii) and (iv).)
claims.proof: We verify hypothesis (H) of Theorem A for F = {f_C : C in CC} (Lemma D). Let S subset of omega^omega with |S| < c and K compact of positive measure. Since b = c there is g with s <=* g for all s in S. Apply (D) to K and h(n) = g(n+1), obtaining B, r, C. Claim: there is an infinite a subset of B with r + chi_a not in C + fin. Suppose not. Identify the power set P(B) with the compact metrizable space 2^B, which has no isolated points. For finite e subset of omega the set Q_e = {a subset of B : r + chi_e + chi_a in C} is closed in P(B) (preimage of C under a continuous map). By assumption every infinite a subset of B lies in some Q_e, so P(B) is the union of the countably many closed sets Q_e and the countably many singletons {a}, a finite. By the Baire category theorem one of these closed sets has nonempty interior; singletons do not, so some Q_e contains a basic open set {a subset of B : a cap F = y} with F a finite subset of B and y subset of F. Then for every b subset of B minus F the set a = y union b lies in Q_e, i.e. r + chi_{e'} + chi_b in C where e' is the symmetric difference of e and y. This contradicts (iv). So fix such a and let x = r + chi_a. By (ii), x in K. By (iii) and Lemma D(b), for n >= 1: f_C(x)(n) > a(n-1) >= B(n-1) >= h(n-1) = g(n) (a subset of B gives a(k) >= B(k)). Hence for every s in S, s(n) <= g(n) < f_C(x)(n) for all but finitely many n, i.e. s <* f_C(x). This is (H). Theorem A gives add(UN) <= |F| <= |CC|.

claims.statement: Lemma T (thin trees are cube-free off a thin set). (1) Let T subset of 2^{<omega} be a tree and 0 = k_{-1} < k_0 < k_1 < ... . There is W subset of omega with |W cap [k_{N-1}, k_N)| <= binom(|T cap 2^{k_N}|, 2) for all N such that the restriction map c -> c|W is injective on [T]. (2) If T is a tree, c -> c|W is injective on [T], r in 2^omega and B subset of omega with B minus W infinite, then there are no finite e, F with r + chi_e + chi_b in [T] for all b subset of B minus F. So condition (iv) of Theorem B holds for C = [T] whenever B minus W is infinite.
claims.proof: (1) For each N >= 0 and each unordered pair of distinct rho, rho' in T cap 2^{k_N} with rho|k_{N-1} = rho'|k_{N-1}, choose p in [k_{N-1}, k_N) with rho(p) != rho'(p); let W be the set of all chosen p. The bound on |W cap [k_{N-1},k_N)| is clear. If c != c' are branches of T, let N be least with c|k_N != c'|k_N; the pair (c|k_N, c'|k_N) was treated, so c and c' differ at a point of W. (2) Suppose r + chi_e + chi_b in [T] for all b subset of B minus F. Pick p in (B minus F) minus W (possible since B minus W is infinite and F finite). The points r + chi_e and r + chi_e + chi_{{p}} are distinct branches of T that agree on W, contradicting injectivity.

claims.statement: Conditional consequence for the Mathias model (does not decide add(UN) there). Let V satisfy CH and let V[G] be the extension by the countable support iteration of Mathias forcing of length omega_2. Assume the standard facts (not re-proved in this work): V[G] satisfies b = c = aleph_2, and V[G_alpha] satisfies CH for alpha < omega_2. Suppose that for some alpha < omega_2 the following holds in V[G]: (D_alpha) for every compact K of positive measure and every h in omega^omega there are an infinite B with B(n) >= h(n), a point r with r + chi_b in K for all b subset of B, and a pair (T, W) in V[G_alpha] (T a tree on 2, W subset of omega, c -> c|W injective on [T]) with r in [T] and B minus W infinite. Then add(UN) = aleph_1 = add(N) in V[G], so the Mathias model would not witness add(N) < add(UN).
claims.proof: 'c -> c|W is injective on [T]' is a Pi^1_1 statement about (T, W), so it holds in V[G] if it holds in V[G_alpha]. Let CC be the family of sets [T] (computed in V[G]) for pairs (T, W) in V[G_alpha] as in (D_alpha); |CC| <= aleph_1 because V[G_alpha] satisfies CH. By Lemma T(2), (D_alpha) gives hypothesis (D) of Theorem B for CC. Since b = c in V[G], Theorem B gives add(UN) <= aleph_1. Also aleph_1 <= add(N) <= add(UN) (Goto's paper, (F3) of the note). Remark, also resting on a standard fact not re-proved here (the Laver property of this iteration over V[G_alpha]): every real r of V[G] lies in [T] for some tree T in V[G_alpha] with |T cap 2^{k_N}| <= N+1, for any prescribed increasing (k_N) in V[G_alpha]; by Lemma T(1) it then has a hitting set W in V[G_alpha] with at most N(N+1)/2 points in [k_{N-1},k_N). Together with Lemma E this shows that all parts of (D_alpha) except 'B minus W is infinite' can always be arranged. Whether that last requirement can be arranged is open (see obstacles).

obstacles: Main gap: I could not prove or refute (D_alpha) in the Mathias model. The set B must be sparse relative to K (Lemma E), and K can be chosen so that the required sparseness function dominates all reals of V[G_alpha]. For such B, a thin ground-model tree can contain a full cube r + chi_e + 2^(B minus F): the count 2^|B cap k_N| <= |T cap 2^(k_N)| is no obstruction. By the Laver property (argument sketched only) every such sparse B is almost contained in a thin ground-model set, so the hitting set W may swallow B. One needs to decouple B from W; the freedom that r may be changed arbitrarily on B was not enough in my attempts (parity tricks reduce to the same problem one level down).

Simplest decoders fail (sketch, not a checked proof): taking C = {c : c|R' = pi|R'} with R', pi in V asks for x in K that agrees with a ground-model real on R' except on a very sparse infinite set. The set of all such x for R' = omega is covered by the null set {z : z o m_0 is constant off a density-zero set}, coded in V[m_0]; so K can avoid it.

Not every candidate point works (sketch): for x = m_0 minus m_1 with m_1 a Mathias real over V[m_0] below (empty, m_0), a compactness argument indicates that every real of V[x] is bounded by a real of V[m_0], so no ground-model Borel map sends x to a real dominating V[m_0]. This relies on continuity of ground-model Borel maps on Mathias cubes, which I did not write out.

g was not computed. In the Mathias model g = aleph_1 iff for some alpha the union of the graphs of Borel functions coded in V[G_alpha], i.e. {(x,y) : y in V[G_alpha][x]}, is non-null. All its sections are null or unions of aleph_1 null sets; I found no argument either way. The route through g and the route through Theorem A both reduce to making a ground-model object pin down information about a real chosen inside an arbitrary later positive compact set.

Option (a) (every union of aleph_1 UN sets is null): no progress. Reflection to stages delta of cofinality omega_1 does not help by itself: V[G_delta] satisfies CH, and the traces of aleph_1 UN sets on V[G_delta] can cover all its reals, which are null in V[G] anyway. The bound add(UN) <= add(SN, N) is probably useless here because the Borel Conjecture is reported to hold in the Mathias model (not checked).

Unverified background used only in the conditional claim and in the obstacle sketches: b = c = aleph_2 and CH at intermediate stages in the Mathias model, the Laver property of the iteration, and the genericity facts about Mathias reals. No source was fetched for these. Galvin-Prikry was avoided (Baire category suffices in Theorem B).

Literature check was brief: one web search found no paper deciding add(UN) (or cov(UN), Goto's Question 6.1) in the Mathias or Laver model. This is not a full search. Theorem A may be folklore-adjacent (it is Reclaw's theorem plus a transfinite recursion); I did not find it stated.

referees.notes:
All seven claims check line by line; I found no broken step. The work is a correct partial result that does not answer Question 6.3 and does not decide add(UN) in the Mathias model, as the author says. Finished 20:35 EST.

**Per-claim check**
- **Claim 1 (Lemma R):** correct. a0 is a limit ordinal, so mu*(Z_{b+1}) = 0 for b < a0. The hull identity mu(E cap H) = mu*(E cap W) is proved correctly. Both Fubini computations run on the Borel set R cap (H x H), and the section-measure sets Y0, X0 are Borel, so no non-measurable set enters a Fubini step.
- **Claim 2 (Theorem A):** correct. The recursion has length c and each stage uses S = {u_d : d < b} of size < c, which (H) allows. R_f is Borel, and it is a strict well-order on X_f because <* is asymmetric and irreflexive. The union meets every positive compact set, so it is not null.
- **Claim 3 (Lemma D):** correct. f_C is Borel, the compactness argument for (a) is right, and (b) follows from Delta_C(x,N) <= |a cap N|.
- **Claim 4 (Lemma E):** correct. I rechecked the count |B cap M_j| <= j-1 for j = 1 and j >= 2, the bound |W_j| 2^{-M_j} <= delta(M_{j-1}), and the sum 1/4 + sum 2^k 8^{-k} = 7/12.
- **Claim 5 (Theorem B):** correct. The Baire argument on 2^B is valid (B infinite, Q_e closed, singletons nowhere dense), and e' = e symmetric-difference y gives the contradiction with (iv). The chain f_C(x)(n) > a(n-1) >= B(n-1) >= h(n-1) = g(n) is right.
- **Claim 6 (Lemma T):** correct, both parts.
- **Claim 7:** correct as a conditional statement. Injectivity of c -> c|W on [T] is Pi^1_1 in (T,W), so it is upward absolute. |CC| <= aleph_1 follows from CH in V[G_alpha]. add(N) = aleph_1 follows from the sandwich aleph_1 <= add(N) <= add(UN) <= aleph_1.

**Consistency tests**
- **MA:** add(UN) = c, so (H) must fail for |F| < c. It does: by tightness each f has a bound g_f off a null set; take S = {g_f + 1} and K outside the union of fewer than add(N) null sets. This also shows (H) forces |F| >= add(N).
- **Countable CC:** (D) must fail in ZFC + b = c. I checked a concrete closed C (each block not all zero): (D) holds for K = 2^omega but fails for K = "each block has at least two ones". No contradiction.
- **Cohen, random, Sacks, Miller:** b < c or b = c = aleph_1, so (H) fails or the bound is trivial.
- **Hechler, Laver:** b = c holds, and nothing known there contradicts the claims.

**Standard facts used in Claim 7 (from memory, not fetched)**
- The Mathias model satisfies b = c = aleph_2.
- V[G_alpha] satisfies CH for alpha < omega_2.
- Mathias forcing has the Laver property, it is preserved by countable support iteration, and the quotient over V[G_alpha] is again such an iteration.
These are textbook facts and I believe them. Claim 7 states the first two as assumptions; the third is used only in the Remark.

**Source checks in flat.txt**
- add(N) <= add(UN) is Corollary 5.13.
- Reference [9] is I. Recław (2001), "On a construction of universally null sets", Real Analysis Exchange 27(1), 321-324, cited as [9, Theorem 1].
- Question 6.1 does ask for cov(UN) in the Laver or Mathias model.
- The Project Euclid URL returned an empty page, so that link is not confirmed.
- The "no prior result" search claim was not re-run.

**Cosmetic points (not errors)**
- In Claim 7, restrict CC to trees with [T] nonempty, since Theorem B needs nonempty closed sets. The trees actually used contain r.
- In the Remark, the slalom bound |T cap 2^{k_0}| <= 1 at N = 0 needs a finite modification of the ground-model slalom.
- (D_alpha) needs one alpha for all K and h. The summary's "ground-model (or V[G_alpha])" should be read that way; letting alpha vary would give |CC| = aleph_2.

**On the open part**
(D_alpha) is not shown consistent or inconsistent. I tried for about ten minutes to refute it and could not. Two observations:
- K_B has the form K' x 2^B, so one may take r|B = 0.
- Its simplest instance (T = {x : x|A = 0}, W = omega minus A) asks whether a positive compact K in V[G] can avoid every x that vanishes on an infinite V[G_alpha] set. Equivalently: is there a countable family J of finite sets with sum 2^{-|a|} < 1 such that every infinite V[G_alpha] set contains a member of J? One Mathias real catches only the sets in its generic ultrafilter. I could not decide this.
Claim 7 may therefore be vacuous; the author's "partial-result" label is accurate.
