Referee 2 report (finished 20:31 EST, deadline 21:40). Files read: local/context.md, notes/partial-results.md, keyword searches in local/flat.txt.

VERDICT: every step of Claims 1-7 checks. I found no false statement and no hole. The claimed status ("partial result, Question 6.3 not answered") is accurate, but see the last section: the "open decoupling statement" appears to be provable, which would decide the Mathias model.

CHECKS PER CLAIM
1. Lemma R. Correct. a0 is a nonzero limit; hull identity mu(E cap H) = mu*(E cap W) is proved correctly and is applied only to Borel E (sections of Borel R); both section-measure functions are Borel, so both Fubini computations are legitimate. No hidden non-measurability: W itself is never integrated over. The statement agrees with Reclaw's theorem as quoted by Goto ("every set well-ordered by a Borel relation is universally null", ref [9], used as [9, Theorem 1]).
2. Theorem A. Correct. Recursion has length c and at stage b uses S of size |b| < c, so (H) applies. u_d <* u_b holds for ALL d < b, so R_f restricted to X_f is exactly the index order; irreflexivity and asymmetry of <* give injectivity. Union meets every positive compact set, hence is non-null. For countable F the hypothesis (H) is simply unsatisfiable, so no conflict with add(UN) >= aleph_1. Model test: under MA, for |F| < c take g_f with f(x) <=* g_f a.e. (tightness), K avoiding the < c null exceptional sets, S = {g_f}; (H) fails, as it must since add(UN) = c there.
3. Lemma D. Correct. Delta_C(x,N) depends on x|N only; (a) is a correct compactness argument; (b) uses Delta_C(x,N) <= |a cap N|.
4. Lemma E. Correct. Arithmetic: 1/4 + sum_{k>=1} 2^k 8^{-k} = 7/12. The index bound |B cap M_j| <= j-1 is right for j = 1 (B cap M_1 empty) and j >= 2. O^(M) is increasing in M and O^(M_0) is empty. Last sentence: B(n) >= M_{n+2} gives |B cap M_{k+1}| <= k-1.
5. Theorem B. Correct. Baire argument on 2^B is valid (Q_e closed, countably many e, no isolated points); e' = e symmetric-difference y. Domination chain s(n) <= g(n) = h(n-1) <= B(n-1) <= a(n-1) < f_C(x)(n) is right. Sanity test: CC = {C} with K = C violates (iv), so no absurd bound add(UN) <= 1.
6. Lemma T. Correct (both parts). k_{-1} = 0 handles N = 0.
7. Conditional Mathias consequence. Correct given the stated standard facts. Injectivity on [T] is Pi^1_1 in (T,W), hence upward absolute; |CC| <= aleph_1 by CH in V[G_alpha]. The Remark is right: the width N+1 version follows from the usual 2^n-slalom form of the Laver property by reindexing (apply it to n -> r|k_{2^{n+1}}).

MINOR NITS (not errors)
- Claim 7: CC should be restricted to trees with nonempty body (needed for f_C); harmless.
- The parameter h in (D_alpha) is redundant: cubes and "B minus W infinite" pass to infinite subsets of B minus W, so B can be thinned to dominate h afterwards.
- With C = [T] and B disjoint from W, the Baire step of Theorem B is not needed: all points r + chi_a (a subset of B) have the same restriction to W, and each [T] + chi_e is injective on W, so [T] + fin contains only countably many of them.
- Standard facts used from memory, not fetched from a primary source: b = c in the Mathias model; CH in V[G_alpha]; Mathias forcing has the Laver property and countable support iteration preserves it (a web search found only secondhand citations to Bartoszynski-Judah, theorem numbers not checked); Borel measurability of section measures.
- Laver model: I believe non(N) = aleph_1 there (from memory, not checked), which would make add(UN) = aleph_1 trivial; only the Mathias model is of interest.

LITERATURE
- Goto's reference [9] is confirmed in flat.txt: I. Reclaw (2001), "On a construction of universally null sets", Real Analysis Exchange 27(1), pp. 321-324. A web search returned the same record at https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.rae/1212763971 (the page itself fetched empty; full text not read).
- Goto's Question 6.1 (cov(UN) in the Laver or Mathias model) and Question 6.3 confirmed in flat.txt.
- One web search found nothing on add(UN) in the Mathias model. Not a full search.

REFEREE'S ADDITION (my own argument, NOT independently reviewed; treat as a claim to be checked)
The decoupling statement left open by the author seems provable in ZFC by a random choice of B.
Proposition. Assume b = c. Let k_N = 2^N and let TT be a family of trees T with |T cap 2^{k_N}| <= N+1 for all N whose bodies cover 2^omega. Then add(UN) <= |TT|.
Proof sketch. For T in TT take W_T from Lemma T(1); then |W_T cap [0,x)| <= (log_2 x + 2)^3. Verify (D) of Theorem B for CC = {[T]}. Given K and h, take s_0 and (M_k) from Lemma E, chosen in addition with M_k >= 2^k and M_{k+1} >= 2 M_k (allowed, since only delta(M_k) <= 8^{-k} 2^{-M_0} is needed). Let B be random: B(n) uniform in [M_{n+2}, M_{n+3}), independently. Every such B is admissible for Lemma E, so lambda(K_B cap [s_0]) >= (5/12) 2^{-M_0}. The set {(B,r) : r in K_B} is closed in the product, so by Fubini there is r with P(r in K_B) > 0. Pick T in TT with r in [T]. P(B(n) in W_T) <= 2 (log_2 M_{n+3} + 2)^3 / M_{n+3} <= 2 (n+5)^3 / 2^{n+3}, which is summable, so by Borel-Cantelli B cap W_T is finite almost surely. Hence some B has r in K_B and B cap W_T finite. Thin B minus W_T to an infinite B' with B'(n) >= h(n). Then (i)-(iii) hold and (iv) holds by Lemma T(2). Theorem B gives add(UN) <= |TT|. The randomness is over B for a fixed r, so the fact that W_T depends on r causes no measurability problem.
Consequence (conditional on the standard facts above): in the Mathias model, ground-model thin trees cover 2^omega (Laver property), there are aleph_1 of them (CH in V), and b = c, so add(UN) = aleph_1 = add(N). So the Mathias model does not witness add(N) < add(UN); option (b) fails there. More generally, any model of b = c in which aleph_1 thin trees cover 2^omega has add(UN) = aleph_1. This is consistent with MA (thin trees are null, so the covering number is >= cov(N) = c) and with add(N) <= add(UN) (the covering number is >= cov(N) >= add(N)). Question 6.3 itself stays open.

attacks.approach: I read context.md, add-UN-note.md and the relevant parts of flat.txt (Sections 2, 3, 5.5, 5.18, 6). I then tried to design countable support (CS) models by analysing which universally null (UN) sets must exist in them. The attempt to make a CS iteration with Cohen reals work failed for a ZFC reason, and that reason is a theorem: if cov(M) = c then add(UN) = add(N). The proof builds add(N) many UN sets with non-null union by a Luzin/Sierpinski-style recursion relative to the sigma-ideal E generated by closed null sets. For the designs that survive (cov(M) < c, e.g. Mathias-type) I give a proved necessary condition and a proved sufficient condition for CS iterations, and list the lemmas that stay open. Literature: a web search found no earlier statement of the theorem (not a full search). I fetched the arXiv record math/9905123 (Bartoszynski, Shelah, "Closed measure zero sets", APAL 58 (1992) 93-110); its abstract only states add(E) <= cov(M) and add(E) = add(M). I do not use that paper; the one direction I need (Claim 1) is proved here.
attacks.summary:
Question 6.3 is not answered. No model of add(N) < add(UN) was built. Finished 20:45 EST.

Main new result (Claim 3, unreviewed): if cov(M) = c, then add(UN) = add(N). More generally this holds if cov(M) = kappa and both N and the closed-null ideal E have cofinal families of size kappa.

Consequences for model design (Claim 4):
- Every model of add(N) < add(UN) has cov(M) < c. So MA(countable), MA(sigma-centered), and every extension that adds Cohen reals cofinally up to c are ruled out. This covers all finite support iterations whose length has cofinality c, not only the sigma-centered and random ones of Goto's Theorem 5.18, and every CS iteration of length omega_2 over CH that adds Cohen reals cofinally.
- With c = aleph_2 the target is now: cov(M) = add(N) = aleph_1 and non(N) = d = g = aleph_2. Mathias-type models are the only CS candidates I see. There add(N) = cov(M), and the proof of Claim 3 breaks at exactly that point (aleph_1 closed null sets can have non-null union).

Lemma list for a CS iteration of length omega_2 over CH (setting (S) of Claim 5):
1. non(N) = aleph_2. Needed. Standard for Mathias-type iterands; not checked here.
2. cov(M) = aleph_1. Needed, by Claim 4 (proved).
3. d = aleph_2 and g = aleph_2. Needed, by add-UN-note.md. d is standard for Mathias; g is OPEN.
4. For every gamma there is beta with E(gamma,beta) Lebesgue null. Needed, by Claim 5 (proved). Whether it holds in any candidate model is OPEN.
5. Property Pi(beta) at a reflecting stage, for every omega_1-family of UN sets. Sufficient, by Claim 6 (proved modulo the standard reflection fact, taken as a hypothesis). Whether any iterand satisfies it is OPEN.

Models with non(N) < c: they need cov(M) < cof(N) (Claim 3) and add(UN) <= cf(non(N)); nothing else was obtained.

Open sub-question: does add(N) < cov(M) alone give add(UN) = add(N)? Claims 1 and 2 need only that. The missing piece is a non-null set X inside the union of the N_j with |X ∩ C| < non(N) for every closed null C. A positive answer would leave only models with add(N) = cov(M).

claims.statement: Claim 1 (small unions of closed null sets). Let E be the sigma-ideal on 2^omega generated by the closed Lebesgue null sets. If theta < cov(M) and {D_i : i < theta} is a family of sets in E, then the union of the D_i is Lebesgue null. In particular every set of size < cov(M) is null, so cov(M) <= non(N).
claims.proof: Each D_i is covered by countably many closed null sets and theta*aleph_0 < cov(M) (the case of finite theta is trivial), so it suffices to treat closed null sets C_i, i < theta. For m in omega let U_m be the countable set of clopen subsets of 2^omega of measure <= 2^-m, with the discrete topology, and let X be the product of the U_m. X is homeomorphic to omega^omega, so fewer than cov(M) meager subsets of X do not cover X (cov(M) is the same for 2^omega and omega^omega; standard). For x = (U_m) in X put N_x = the set of y lying in U_m for infinitely many m. Then lambda(N_x) <= inf_k sum_{m>=k} 2^-m = 0. For a closed null C let G_C be the set of x such that C is a subset of U_m for infinitely many m. For each m the set {x : C subset U_m} is clopen in X, so G_C is a G_delta. G_C is dense: given a finite prefix U_0..U_{l-1} and k, take m >= max(k,l); C is compact and null, so an open set of measure < 2^-m covers it, and finitely many basic clopen subsets of that open set cover C; their union is a clopen set of measure <= 2^-m, which we take as U_m. If x is in G_C then C is a subset of N_x. The complements of the G_{C_i} are theta < cov(M) meager sets, so some x lies in all G_{C_i}, and then all C_i are subsets of the null set N_x. Singletons are closed null sets, which gives the last sentence.

claims.statement: Claim 2 (dense trace lemma). Call a closed set Q self-supporting if Q is nonempty and lambda(Q ∩ [s]) > 0 whenever Q ∩ [s] is nonempty. Assume theta := add(N) < cov(M). Then there are null G_delta sets N_j (j < theta) such that every closed set P of positive measure contains a self-supporting closed set Q for which, for some j, N_j ∩ Q is dense in Q.
claims.proof:
Step 0. Take null sets M_i (i < theta) with non-null union and null G_delta supersets M_i'. Let {N_j : j < theta} list all translates M_i' + e, where e ranges over the countable group Fin of finitely supported elements of 2^omega. Each N_j is a null G_delta. Their union Y is Fin-invariant and not null. Y meets every closed P of positive measure: otherwise Y is a subset of H = the intersection over e in Fin of ((2^omega minus P) + e), a Fin-invariant Borel set of measure < 1; by the 0-1 law lambda(H) = 0, so Y is null, a contradiction.

Step 1. For closed F let F* = F minus the union of all [s] with lambda(F ∩ [s]) = 0. Then F* is closed, F minus F* is a countable union of closed null sets, and F* is empty or self-supporting: if F* ∩ [s] is nonempty then lambda(F ∩ [s]) > 0 and lambda(F* ∩ [s]) = lambda(F ∩ [s]).

Step 2. Fix closed P of positive measure and suppose no pair (j, Q) as in the claim exists with Q subset of P. Fix j. Define closed sets by F_0 = cl(N_j ∩ P), F_{xi+1} = cl(N_j ∩ (F_xi)*), and intersections at limits. Since F_{xi+1} is a subset of (F_xi)*, the sequence is decreasing, and a decreasing omega_1-sequence of closed subsets of 2^omega is eventually constant (for each basic [s] record the first index at which F_xi misses [s]; take the supremum xi_0 of these countably many indices). So F := F_{xi_0} = F_{xi_0+1} = cl(N_j ∩ F*), which is a subset of F*, hence F = F*. If F is nonempty, then F is self-supporting, F is a subset of P, and N_j ∩ F is dense in F, contradicting the supposition. So F is empty. Now let x be in N_j ∩ P. Then x is in F_0. The least xi with x not in F_xi exists, is not 0, and is not a limit, so xi = zeta+1 with x in F_zeta and x not in cl(N_j ∩ (F_zeta)*). As x is in N_j, x is not in (F_zeta)*. Hence N_j ∩ P is a subset of the union over zeta <= xi_0 of (F_zeta minus (F_zeta)*), a countable union of closed null sets. So N_j ∩ P is in E for every j.

Step 3. Then Y ∩ P is a union of theta < cov(M) sets in E, so it is null by Claim 1. Take a null G_delta set H containing Y ∩ P. P minus H has positive measure, so it contains a closed set P' of positive measure, and P' misses Y. This contradicts Step 0.

claims.statement: Claim 3 (main theorem). Let kappa = cov(M). Assume (i) there is a family of kappa null sets cofinal in N, and (ii) there is a family {D_alpha : alpha < kappa} of sets in E such that every closed null set is contained in some D_alpha. Then add(UN) = add(N). Both hypotheses hold when cov(M) = c. So: cov(M) = c implies add(UN) = add(N).
claims.proof:
Standard facts used: (a) for an atomless finite nonzero Borel measure mu on 2^omega there is a Borel bijection phi of 2^omega carrying mu/mu(2^omega) to lambda; hence add and non of the mu-null ideal equal add(N) and non(N); (b) Lebesgue decomposition and inner regularity by closed sets; (c) a nonempty closed subset of 2^omega without isolated points is homeomorphic to 2^omega.

add(N) <= add(UN): by (a), a union of fewer than add(N) UN sets is mu-null for every atomless mu. Also add(UN) <= non(N), since a non-null set of size non(N) is a union of non(N) singletons.

non(N) = kappa: kappa <= non(N) by Claim 1. If non(N) > kappa, choose for each member H of the cofinal family in (i) a point outside H; these at most kappa points form a null set, which lies in some member H', contradicting the choice for H'. Also cf(kappa) > omega, because a set of size non(N) that is a countable union of smaller sets is null.

Let theta = add(N). If theta >= kappa then theta <= add(UN) <= non(N) = kappa <= theta and we are done. Assume theta < kappa. Take N_j (j < theta) from Claim 2. By (i) fix null G_delta sets H_alpha (alpha < kappa) cofinal in N. Fix D_alpha as in (ii).

Recursion on alpha < kappa. Choose a closed P_alpha of positive measure disjoint from H_alpha. By Claim 2 choose j_alpha < theta and a self-supporting closed Q_alpha inside P_alpha with N_{j_alpha} ∩ Q_alpha dense in Q_alpha. Q_alpha has no isolated points (points are null), so by (c) it is a copy of 2^omega. N_{j_alpha} ∩ Q_alpha is a dense G_delta in Q_alpha, so its complement in Q_alpha is meager. Each D_delta ∩ Q_alpha is meager in Q_alpha: a closed null set contains no nonempty relatively open subset of the self-supporting Q_alpha, so it is nowhere dense there. Since |alpha| < kappa = cov(M), fewer than cov(M) meager sets are involved, so we can pick x_alpha in N_{j_alpha} ∩ Q_alpha outside every D_delta, delta < alpha.

For j < theta let A_j = {x_alpha : j_alpha = j}, a subset of N_j.

The union of the A_j is not null: a null set lies in some H_alpha, but x_alpha is in P_alpha, which is disjoint from H_alpha.

Each A_j is UN. Let mu be an atomless finite Borel measure, mu = mu_ac + mu_s with mu_ac << lambda and mu_s concentrated on a Borel lambda-null set Z. By inner regularity take closed C_n inside Z with mu_s(Z minus the union of the C_n) = 0. Each C_n is closed null, so C_n is a subset of D_{delta_n} for some delta_n; let delta* = sup delta_n < kappa. If alpha > delta_n then x_alpha is not in D_{delta_n}. So A_j ∩ (union of the C_n) is a subset of {x_alpha : alpha <= delta*}, of size < kappa = non(N), hence mu-null by (a). The rest of A_j lies in the Borel set N_j minus the union of the C_n, whose mu-measure is at most mu_ac(N_j) + mu_s(2^omega minus the union of the C_n) = 0. So mu*(A_j) = 0.

Thus theta UN sets have a union that is not null, hence not UN, and add(UN) <= theta = add(N).

The case cov(M) = c: (i) holds with all null G_delta sets (there are c of them) and (ii) holds with an enumeration of all closed null sets.

Not proved here: that (ii) follows from (i) in general. I expect this from Bartoszynski's slalom characterisation of cof(N), which I did not fetch; the statement 'cov(M) = cof(N) implies add(UN) = add(N)' is therefore marked unproved.

claims.statement: Claim 4 (design constraints). (a) Any model of add(N) < add(UN) satisfies cov(M) < c. (b) MA(countable) and MA(sigma-centered) each imply add(UN) = add(N). (c) In a CS iteration of length omega_2 over a model of CH in which every real appears at a stage < omega_2 and cofinally many stages add a Cohen real over the previous model, add(UN) = add(N).
claims.proof: (a) is the contrapositive of Claim 3. (b) MA(countable) is equivalent to cov(M) = c, and MA(sigma-centered) implies MA(countable) (standard); apply Claim 3. (c) In the extension c = aleph_2. Given aleph_1 meager sets, their Borel codes appear by some stage beta < omega_2; a Cohen real added later over a model containing these codes avoids all of them. So cov(M) = aleph_2 = c and Claim 3 applies. The same argument covers finite support iterations of nontrivial posets whose length has cofinality c in the extension, using the standard fact (not proved here) that such iterations add Cohen reals at limit stages of countable cofinality.

claims.statement: Claim 5 (necessary condition for CS-type models). Setting (S): in the universe W, non(N) = c = aleph_2, and there is an increasing chain of transitive ZFC models V_beta (beta < omega_2) whose reals have union 2^omega, each with at most aleph_1 reals. For gamma <= beta let E(gamma,beta) be the set of z in 2^omega for which there is a Borel set R in the plane, coded in V_gamma, with every section R^z' = {y : (y,z') in R} null, such that every real of V_beta lies in R^z. Then: (1) the outer measure of E(gamma,beta) is 0 or 1; (2) if for some gamma the set E(gamma,beta) is non-null for every beta, then add(UN) = aleph_1. Hence add(UN) = aleph_2 requires: for every gamma there is beta with E(gamma,beta) null.
claims.proof:
(1) If z is in E(gamma,beta) via R and e is finitely supported, then z+e is in E(gamma,beta) via R' = {(y,x) : (y,x+e) in R}, which is coded in V_gamma and has null sections. So E is Fin-invariant. Let H be a G_delta superset of E with lambda(H) = lambda*(E), and H' the intersection of all H+e. H' is Borel, Fin-invariant, contains E, and has the same measure, which is 0 or 1 by the 0-1 law.

(2) Let Rel be the set of Borel sets coded in V_gamma with all sections null; it has size at most aleph_1. Enumerate 2^omega as y_alpha and the compact sets of positive measure as C_alpha (alpha < omega_2). For each alpha pick beta(alpha) >= gamma with {y_delta : delta < alpha} inside V_{beta(alpha)}; this is possible since the set has size at most aleph_1. E(gamma,beta(alpha)) has outer measure 1, so pick z_alpha in it and in C_alpha, with witness R_alpha in Rel. For R in Rel put A_R = {z_alpha : R_alpha = R}. A_R is UN: let mu be atomless. By Fubini, (lambda x mu)(R) is the integral of lambda(R^z) d mu(z) = 0, so for lambda-almost every y the set R_y = {z : (y,z) in R} is mu-null; pick such y = y_delta. If alpha > delta and R_alpha = R then y_delta is a real of V_{beta(alpha)}, so y_delta is in R^{z_alpha}, that is z_alpha is in R_{y_delta}. Hence A_R is a subset of R_{y_delta} together with {z_alpha : alpha <= delta}; the second set has size at most aleph_1 < non(N), so it is mu-null. The union of the A_R meets every compact set of positive measure, so it is not null. Thus aleph_1 UN sets have a non-UN union.

This is the criterion (‡) of context.md specialised to a chain of models, together with the 0-1 law.

claims.statement: Claim 6 (sufficient condition for CS-type models). Assume setting (S) of Claim 5. Let F in W be a function sending each pair (mu, i), mu an atomless finite Borel measure and i < omega_1, to a code of a mu-null Borel set B^i_mu. Suppose beta < omega_2 is such that the restriction of F to measures in V_beta belongs to V_beta, and the following property Pi(beta) holds for that restriction: the set T of z not in V_beta such that for some i, z lies in B^i_mu for every atomless mu in V_beta, is Lebesgue null in W. Then the union over i of the kernels K_i = the intersection over all mu of B^i_mu is Lebesgue null. Consequently, if for every omega_1-family of UN sets such F and beta can be found (F with A_i inside every B^i_mu), then add(UN) = aleph_2.
claims.proof:
If z is in K_i and not in V_beta, then z is in B^i_mu for every mu in V_beta, so z is in T. So the union of the K_i is contained in T together with the reals of V_beta. The latter set has size at most aleph_1 < non(N), so it is null, and T is null by Pi(beta).

For the consequence: let A_i (i < omega_1) be UN. Choose F with A_i inside B^i_mu for all mu. Then A_i is inside K_i, so the union of the A_i is null. So every omega_1-union of UN sets is null. It is then UN: for atomless mu take the Borel bijection phi carrying the normalised mu to lambda; the sets phi[A_i] are UN, so their union is lambda-null, so the union of the A_i is mu-null. Hence add(UN) >= aleph_2, and add(UN) <= non(N) = aleph_2.

Not proved here: that in a CS iteration of proper posets of size aleph_1 over CH, for every F there are stationarily many beta of cofinality omega_1 with F restricted to V_beta in V_beta. Goto's Claim 3.3.1 asserts this kind of reflection as standard. Whether Pi(beta) holds for any iterand is open.

obstacles: No model of add(N) < add(UN) was constructed, and Question 6.3 stays open.

Claim 3 has not been reviewed by anyone else. It is a ZFC theorem that would also strengthen Goto's Theorem 5.18 in the cases with cov(M) = c, so it should get an independent check before it is relied on.
The method of Claim 3 stops at add(N) = cov(M): Step 3 of Claim 2 needs a union of add(N) many closed null sets to be null. In the Mathias model add(N) = cov(M) = aleph_1, so that model is untouched.

The recursion in Claim 3 needs a family cofinal in N and a family cofinal for closed null sets, both of size cov(M). I proved this only for cov(M) = c. The extension to cov(M) = cof(N) depends on a slalom characterisation of cof(N) that I did not fetch.

For Mathias-type CS iterations three lemmas are open: g = aleph_2; E(gamma,beta) null for some beta (necessary, Claim 5); Pi(beta) (sufficient, Claim 6). I could not decide the one-step version: for r Mathias over V and w random over V[r], is the set of reals of V[w] null in V[r][w]? A random real splits r, so the unsplit-real null set does not work.

The Larson-Zapletal measured-extension method gives that UN sets live in an intermediate model. I believe, but did not verify, that measured extensions keep the ground reals non-null; if so the method cannot be used directly when non(N) must grow.

Models with non(N) < c need techniques other than CS iteration over CH, since those give c <= aleph_2 = non(N) in the relevant cases. I obtained only the constraints cov(M) < cof(N) and add(UN) <= cf(non(N)) for them.
Literature check was brief: one web search and one arXiv record fetch. Novelty of Claim 3 is not established.

errors: Claim 4(c), step 'In the extension c = aleph_2': not justified by the stated hypotheses. The argument needs omega_2^V to stay a regular cardinal and to equal c in the extension. This holds for proper iterands with dense subsets of size <= aleph_1 (each V_beta then satisfies CH and the iteration is aleph_2-cc), but that hypothesis is missing. Without it (e.g. a first iterand adding aleph_3 reals) the argument only gives cov(M) >= aleph_2, possibly < c, and Claim 3 does not apply. Repair: add the hypothesis 'proper iterands of size <= aleph_1' or 'c = aleph_2 and omega_2 is preserved'. The same caveat applies to the summary line 'every CS iteration of length omega_2 over CH that adds Cohen reals cofinally'.

Claim 4(c), last sentence, and the summary line 'all finite support iterations whose length has cofinality c': the step 'their Borel codes appear by some stage beta' needs every real to appear at a stage below the length. That is true for ccc iterations of length of uncountable cofinality but is not given for arbitrary 'nontrivial posets'. Repair: say 'ccc' (or theta-cc with cf(length) >= theta, as in Goto's Theorem 5.18).

Summary line 'Models with non(N) < c: they need cov(M) < cof(N) (Claim 3)': this uses the implication (i) => (ii), which the author marks unproved inside Claim 3. So the summary overstates what Claim 3 proves. Repair (short, modulo one standard theorem that I did not fetch): by Bartoszynski's slalom characterisation, cof(N) is the least size of a family of slaloms S with |S(n)| <= n+1 such that every f in omega^omega has f(n) in S(n) for all but finitely many n. Let U_n be the countable set of clopen sets of measure <= 4^-n. For a slalom S with S(n) a subset of U_n put D_S = union over k of the intersection over n >= k of the union of S(n). Each inner intersection is closed of measure <= inf (n+1)4^-n = 0, so D_S is in E. A closed null C is compact, so C is a subset of some f(n) in U_n for each n; if S captures f from k on, then C is a subset of D_S. Hence cof(N) = kappa gives (ii).

referees.notes:
Verdict: the main mathematics is correct. I checked every step of Claims 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 and found no error. The gaps are in Claim 4(c) and in two summary lines, and all are repairable by adding hypotheses or a short argument (see errors). Review done 20:36 EST.

What I checked, claim by claim.

Claim 1 (fewer than cov(M) sets in E have null union): correct. The sets {x : C subset x(m)} depend on one coordinate, so they are clopen; G_C is a dense G_delta; N_x is null by Borel-Cantelli; theta*aleph_0 < cov(M). A search snippet says Bartoszynski-Shelah prove add(E,N) = cov(M), so this direction is probably known; I could not read the PDF (no PDF tools here), so that is not checked.

Claim 2 (dense trace lemma): correct. Step 0: the 0-1 law is applied to a Fin-invariant Borel set of measure <= 1 - lambda(P) < 1. Step 1: F* is closed and empty or self-supporting. attacks.approach: Read context.md, add-UN-note.md and the relevant parts of flat.txt (Claim 5.5.1, Fact 5.10, Lemma 5.11, Proposition 5.12, Grzegorek citation). I first tried to keep the note's shear (c,w) -> (c + w∘h, w) and replace the length-c recursion by Fubini, elementary submodels and club guessing. All of these fail at one point: the set of good w, T(K,c,h) = {w : (c + w∘h, w) in K}, depends on the code c, so one new point is needed for each compact K (cof(N) many). The fix is to drop the shear. Write the code c on a sparse coordinate set B_h = ran(h) and an arbitrary real u on the other coordinates (the homeomorphism m_h). For h sparse enough for K, K contains a positive closed set that is invariant under all changes on B_h. So the set of good u no longer depends on c, and one fixed graph from a Grzegorek set onto a set of full outer measure serves every K. No recursion and no hypothesis on c are needed.
attacks.summary:
I get a proof that ZFC proves add(UN) <= d, with no hypothesis (Claims 1 and 2). This removes "there is a universally null set of size c" from the theorem in add-UN-note.md. It does not answer Question 6.3, because add(N) <= d also holds. I checked each step by hand; no second reviewer and no formal proof exists.

Method: for strictly increasing h with co-infinite range let m_h(c,u) be the real that equals c along ran(h) and u along the complement. Take P = {c_beta} universally null of size non(N) (Grzegorek, as cited by Goto), Y = {y_beta} of full outer measure and size non(N), and Gamma = {(c_beta, y_beta)}. Gamma is universally null by Goto's Claim 5.5.1, so each m_h[Gamma] is universally null. For a dominating family D, the union of the m_h[Gamma] meets every compact set of positive measure.

Further results: the bound is really add(UN) <= theta_inv <= d for a coordinate-set invariant theta_inv, and add(E,N) <= theta_inv, so this method cannot go below add(E,N) (Claim 3). Two side results: a set with universally null projection and universally null vertical sections is universally null (Claim 4); and add(UN) <= g if there is a universally null set of size cof(N), in particular if non(N) = cof(N) (Claim 5).

Consequence for Question 6.3: a model of add(N) < add(UN) needs add(N) < add(UN) <= min(d, cf(non(N))). A brief web search found no earlier statement of add(UN) <= d; this is not a full literature search.

claims.statement: Lemma 1 (invariant subsets). Notation: lambda is the product measure on 2^omega. For B a subset of omega and x in 2^omega put [x]_B = {y : y(j) = x(j) for all j not in B}. Let K be a compact subset of 2^omega with lambda(K) > 0. Then there are s_0 in 2^{<omega} and a strictly increasing sequence b_0 < b_1 < ... of natural numbers such that for every set B whose k-th element (in increasing order) is >= b_k for all k, the set Good = {x in [s_0] : [x]_B is a subset of K} is closed, is a subset of K, is B-invariant (x in Good and y in [x]_B imply y in Good), and has lambda(Good) >= (1/4) 2^{-|s_0|} > 0.
claims.proof:
Step 1 (density). There is s_0 with lambda(K cap [s_0]) > (1/2) 2^{-|s_0|}. Otherwise take open V containing K with lambda(V) < 2 lambda(K), write V as a disjoint union of cylinders [s_j]; then lambda(K) = sum_j lambda(K cap [s_j]) <= (1/2) lambda(V) < lambda(K), a contradiction. Put l = |s_0|.

Step 2 (levels). U = [s_0] minus K is open and lambda(U) < (1/2) 2^{-l}. Write U as the disjoint union of the cylinders [s_i], i in I, where the s_i are the inclusion-minimal strings with [s_i] a subset of U. Each s_i properly extends s_0 (because [s_i] is inside [s_0] and U is not all of [s_0]). So sum_i 2^{-|s_i|} = lambda(U). For m in omega put a_m = sum of 2^{-|s_i|} over the i with |s_i| = m, and t(n) = sum_{m > n} a_m. Then t(n) -> 0. Choose b_0 < b_1 < ... with b_0 >= l and t(b_k) <= 4^{-k-2} 2^{-l} for all k. Put N(m) = |{k : b_k < m}|. So N(m) = 0 for m <= b_0 and N(m) = k+1 for b_k < m <= b_{k+1}.

Step 3 (estimate). Let B be as in the statement. Then |B cap m| <= N(m) for every m (if the k-th element of B is < m then b_k < m), and B cap l is empty because b_0 >= l. So [x]_B is a subset of [s_0] for x in [s_0]. For x in [s_0] and i in I: [x]_B meets [s_i] if and only if x(j) = s_i(j) for all j < |s_i| with j not in B. (If the condition holds, change x on B cap |s_i| to agree with s_i; the result is in [x]_B and in [s_i]. The converse is clear.) The set E_i of all x with x(j) = s_i(j) for all j in |s_i| minus B is clopen with lambda(E_i) = 2^{-(|s_i| - |B cap |s_i||)}, and E_i is inside [s_0]. Let Bad be the union of the E_i. Then Bad is open and
lambda(Bad) <= sum_i 2^{-|s_i|} 2^{|B cap |s_i||} <= sum_m a_m 2^{N(m)} <= sum_{m <= b_0} a_m + sum_{k >= 0} 2^{k+1} t(b_k) < (1/2) 2^{-l} + sum_{k >= 0} 2^{k+1} 4^{-k-2} 2^{-l} = 2^{-l} (1/2 + 1/4).
So Good = [s_0] minus Bad is closed with lambda(Good) > (1/4) 2^{-l}. By the equivalence above, Good = {x in [s_0] : [x]_B cap U is empty} = {x in [s_0] : [x]_B is a subset of K cap [s_0]}, which is the set in the statement. Since x is in [x]_B, Good is a subset of K. If x is in Good and y is in [x]_B then y is in [s_0] and [y]_B = [x]_B, so y is in Good.

claims.statement: Theorem 2 (ZFC). add(UN) <= d. Here UN is the ideal of universally null subsets of 2^omega and d is the dominating number. No hypothesis on the existence of a universally null set of size c is needed.
claims.proof:
Facts used, all stated in Goto, arXiv:2607.12936v4 (text checked in flat.txt). (F1) Lemma 5.11 and Fact 5.10: UN is invariant under Borel isomorphisms; below only the direct push-forward argument is used. (F2) Claim 5.5.1: if X is in UN and f : X -> 2^omega is any function, the graph {(x, f(x)) : x in X} is universally null in 2^omega x 2^omega. (F3) Grzegorek's theorem, as cited by Goto as reference [6]: there is a universally null set of cardinality non(N).

The family D. Let D_0 be a dominating family of size d. Close it under finite modifications, replace each g by n -> max_{i<=n} g(i) + n, and then replace each resulting h by n -> 2h(n) + 1. This gives a family D of size d of strictly increasing functions with odd values such that every F in omega^omega satisfies F(n) <= h(n) for all n for some h in D. For h in D, ran(h) is infinite and its complement contains all even numbers. Let g_h enumerate omega minus ran(h) increasingly.

The maps m_h. Define m_h : 2^omega x 2^omega -> 2^omega by m_h(c,u)(h(n)) = c(n) and m_h(c,u)(g_h(n)) = u(n). This is a homeomorphism induced by a bijection of coordinates, so it sends lambda x lambda to lambda.

The set Gamma. Let kappa = non(N). By (F3) fix P = {c_beta : beta < kappa} in UN, enumerated without repetition. Fix a non-null X of size kappa and put Y = X + Q, where Q is the countable group of finite-support elements. Then |Y| = kappa and Y has full outer measure: if A is Borel and contains Y, then A' = the intersection of the A + q (q in Q) is Borel, Q-invariant and contains X, so lambda(A') > 0; a Borel set invariant under all finite changes is a tail event, so lambda(A') = 1 by the Kolmogorov 0-1 law, hence lambda(A) = 1. Enumerate Y = {y_beta : beta < kappa} and put Gamma = {(c_beta, y_beta) : beta < kappa}. Gamma is the graph of a function on P, so Gamma is universally null in the plane by (F2).

Each W_h = m_h[Gamma] is in UN. Let mu be an atomless finite Borel measure on 2^omega. Its push-forward under the inverse of m_h is an atomless finite Borel measure on the plane, so Gamma has outer measure zero for it, so m_h[Gamma] has mu-outer measure zero.

The union W of the W_h (h in D) is not null. Let K be compact with lambda(K) > 0. Take s_0 and (b_k) from Lemma 1 and h in D with h(k) >= b_k for all k. Then B = ran(h) satisfies the hypothesis of Lemma 1, so Good = {x in [s_0] : [x]_B is a subset of K} is closed, B-invariant, inside K, and has positive measure. Put G = {u : m_h(c,u) is in Good for some c}. Since m_h(c,u) and m_h(c',u) differ only on B, B-invariance gives that the preimage of Good under m_h equals 2^omega x G. So G is closed and lambda(G) = (lambda x lambda)(2^omega x G) = lambda(Good) > 0. Y has full outer measure, so some y_beta is in G. Then m_h(c_beta, y_beta) is in Good, hence in K, and it is in W_h. So W meets every compact set of positive measure. If W were null, there would be an open set containing W of measure < 1, and its complement would be a compact set of positive measure disjoint from W. So W is not null, hence not universally null.

Thus D indexes d universally null sets with a union that is not universally null, so add(UN) <= d.

claims.statement: Corollary 3 (sharper form and a limit of the method). Let theta_inv be the least size of a family BB of infinite co-infinite subsets of omega such that for every compact K of positive measure there is B in BB for which {x : [x]_B is a subset of K} has positive measure. Let E be the ideal generated by closed null sets and add(E,N) the least number of sets in E whose union is not null. Then add(E,N) <= theta_inv <= d and add(UN) <= theta_inv.
claims.proof:
theta_inv <= d: the family {ran(h) : h in D} from the proof of Theorem 2 works by Lemma 1, because Good is a subset of {x : [x]_B is a subset of K}; that set is closed, hence measurable.

add(UN) <= theta_inv: repeat the proof of Theorem 2 with BB in place of {ran(h)}. For B in BB let m_B(c,u) be the real that equals c along the increasing enumeration of B and u along the increasing enumeration of the complement; put W_B = m_B[Gamma]. Each W_B is in UN as before. Given K, take B in BB with S = {x : [x]_B is a subset of K} of positive measure. S is B-invariant, so its preimage under m_B is 2^omega x G with G measurable and lambda(G) = lambda(S) > 0. Pick y_beta in G; then m_B(c_beta, y_beta) is in S, and S is a subset of K. So the union of the W_B meets every compact set of positive measure and is not null.

add(E,N) <= theta_inv: for B in BB let L_B = {x : x(j) = 0 for all j in B}. L_B is closed and null because B is infinite. Given compact K of positive measure, take B in BB and x with [x]_B a subset of K; the element y of [x]_B that is 0 on B lies in K and in L_B. So the union of the L_B (B in BB) meets every compact set of positive measure and is not null.

Remark, not proved here: add(E,N) = cov(M) is attributed in my memory to Bartoszynski and Shelah; this was not checked. If it holds, the coordinate-set method cannot give a bound below cov(M).

claims.statement: Lemma 4 (sections). Let Gamma be a subset of 2^omega x 2^omega. If the projection of Gamma to the first coordinate is universally null and every vertical section Gamma_x = {z : (x,z) in Gamma} is universally null, then Gamma is universally null in the plane. In particular the product of two universally null sets is universally null, and Goto's Claim 5.5.1 is the case of one-point sections. This lemma is not used in Theorem 2.
claims.proof: Let mu be an atomless finite Borel measure on the plane and nu(A) = mu(A x 2^omega) its first marginal. The set D of atoms of nu is countable, and nu_0(A) = nu(A minus D) is an atomless finite Borel measure (possibly zero). The projection of Gamma is universally null, so there is a Borel set A containing it with nu_0(A) = 0, that is, mu((A minus D) x 2^omega) = 0. For each a in D the measure mu_a(C) = mu({a} x C) is finite, Borel and atomless, because mu has no point masses. So there is a Borel C_a containing Gamma_a with mu({a} x C_a) = 0. Gamma is a subset of ((A minus D) x 2^omega) together with the countably many sets {a} x C_a (a in D). This is a Borel set of mu-measure zero.

claims.statement: Proposition 5 (hypothesis of the note weakened in the g-form). Let g be the least size of a family of Borel functions 2^omega -> 2^omega whose graphs {(f(w), w)} have a non-null union in the plane. If there is a universally null set of cardinality cof(N), then add(UN) <= g. In particular this holds whenever non(N) = cof(N). The note needed a universally null set of size c. By the note's Lemma, g <= d; that Lemma is not re-proved in this claim.
claims.proof:
Let FF be a family of g Borel functions whose graphs have non-null union. Close FF under f -> (w -> f(w + b) + a) for finite-support a, b; the size stays g because g is uncountable (g >= add(N)). The graph of the new function is graph(f) + (a,b), so the union U of all graphs is invariant under translation by Q x Q, where Q is the group of finite-support elements.

U meets every compact K in the plane of positive measure: if not, U is disjoint from every K + q (q in Q x Q), hence from their union K*, which is Borel, Q x Q-invariant and of positive measure, so of measure 1 by the 0-1 law; then U is null, a contradiction.

The interleaving homeomorphism carries lambda x lambda to lambda, so the null ideal of the plane has a cofinal family {G_xi : xi < cof(N)} of Borel null sets. For each xi pick a compact K_xi of positive measure disjoint from G_xi. A set that meets every K_xi is not null, since a null set lies inside some G_xi.

Let P = {c_xi : xi < cof(N)} be universally null, enumerated without repetition. For each xi the compact set K_xi + (c_xi, 0) has positive measure, so there are f_xi in FF and w_xi with (f_xi(w_xi), w_xi) in K_xi + (c_xi, 0). Put q_xi = (c_xi + f_xi(w_xi), w_xi); it lies in K_xi. For f in FF let sigma_f(c,w) = (c + f(w), w); this is a Borel bijection of the plane and its own inverse. Let Gamma_f = {(c_xi, w_xi) : f_xi = f}. Gamma_f is part of the graph of the function c_xi -> w_xi on P, so it is universally null by Goto's Claim 5.5.1. Then sigma_f[Gamma_f] is universally null: push any atomless measure forward under sigma_f, which is its own inverse. The union over f in FF of the sets sigma_f[Gamma_f] is {q_xi : xi < cof(N)}, which meets every K_xi and so is not null. Transport to 2^omega by the interleaving homeomorphism. So g universally null sets have a union that is not universally null.

If non(N) = cof(N), Grzegorek's theorem (as cited by Goto) gives a universally null set of that size.

obstacles: Question 6.3 is not answered. Theorem 2 gives add(N) <= add(UN) <= min(d, cf(non(N))), and add(N) <= d holds anyway. A model of add(N) < add(UN) is still possible wherever add(N) < d and add(N) < non(N), for example possibly the Mathias model.

The coordinate-set method cannot go below add(E,N) (Claim 3). The leaves {x : x restricted to B = c} are closed null sets. To reach add(N) one would need Borel, non-closed foliations: a family Phi of measure-preserving Borel isomorphisms phi from the plane to the line such that every positive compact K contains phi[2^omega x G] for some phi in Phi and positive G. The same proof gives add(UN) <= |Phi| for any such family. I know only |Phi| >= add(N) for such families. Whether |Phi| = add(N) is possible is open, and it would settle Question 6.3.

Exact failure point of the routes suggested in the task (Lemma B with a Grzegorek set, elementary submodels of size non(N), sections P + {w o h}): with the shear (c,w) -> (c + w o h, w) the set T(K,c,h) of good w depends on c. Section-wise Fubini reduces the problem to itself: P + E non-null with |E| <= d is already the statement add(UN) <= d. Theorem 2 avoids this because m_h makes the set of good u independent of c.

An unconditional bound add(UN) <= g was not obtained; the uniformity in c that makes Theorem 2 work is not available for arbitrary Borel graphs. Whether add(UN) <= b or add(UN) <= cov(M) holds in ZFC is not settled here.

attacks.summary:
Question 6.3 is not settled in full, but the cardinal g is: ZFC proves g = add(N) (Claim 1). So the answers to the four questions are: (1) yes, g = add(N), and the partial-functions-on-null-sets idea works; (2) g <= b, non(M), cov(M), add*(N) all hold, since g = add(N); (3) inf over perfect Psi of i(Psi) = add(N), attained at the closed subgroup {0} x 2^omega, not by a Mycielski argument (Claim 5); (4) g > add(N) is not consistent.

Consequence for Question 6.3 (Claim 2): if there is a universally null set of size at least cof(N), then add(UN) = add(N). By Grzegorek's theorem (as quoted in context.md) this holds whenever non(N) = cof(N), in particular whenever non(N) = c; it also holds whenever a UN set of size c exists (Miller model). So a model of add(N) < add(UN) must satisfy non(N) < cof(N) and have no UN set of size cof(N).

Side results (Claim 4): for continuous functions the analogous cardinal g_c satisfies cov(M) <= g_c, and the 'almost everywhere' variant g* (which I argue equals non(N) after one random real) satisfies cov(M) <= g* <= min(d, non(N)). In the Cohen model g = aleph_1 < g_c = g* = c. So g is not non(N) of the one-random-real extension, contrary to the expectation in context.md.

claims.statement: Claim 1 (ZFC). g = add(N). More precisely there are a Borel map phi : omega^omega x 2^omega -> 2^omega and a function H : omega -> omega\{0} such that for every compact K in 2^omega x 2^omega with positive measure there is a slalom S_K (S_K(n) a subset of omega with at most H(n) elements) with: whenever f(n) is not in S_K(n) for infinitely many n, the graph of phi_f = phi(f,.) meets K. Consequently there is a family of at most add(N) Borel functions 2^omega -> 2^omega whose graphs have a union meeting every compact set of positive measure (full outer measure). Each phi_f is constantly 0 outside a null Borel set N_f, so the 'partial Borel functions on null Borel domains' scheme of Question (1) works with add(N) functions.
claims.proof:
Notation. lambda is the product measure on 2^omega, lambda^2 on the plane. For a finite or infinite set J of coordinates, 2^J carries the product measure.

Step 0 (codes). Let T = {(s,t) : s,t in 2^{<omega}, |s|=|t|}. For a in 2^T put K_a = {(w,v) : a(w|n, v|n) = 1 for all n}, a closed subset of the plane. Every closed K equals K_a for a = indicator of {(s,t) : K meets [s]x[t]}. Define Psi(a,w) = the lexicographically least element of the section (K_a)_w if it is nonempty, and 0^omega otherwise. Psi is Borel: by compactness, (K_a)_w meets [t] iff for every m >= |t| some t' in 2^m extending t has a(w|n,t'|n)=1 for all n <= m, a closed condition on (a,w); the least element is then computed bit by bit.

Step 1 (parameters, independent of K). Define by recursion kappa_{-1} = 1 and, for n >= 0: r_n = the least integer with 2^n 2^{-r_n} <= 2^{-2n-4} kappa_{n-1}; rho_n = 2^{-r_n}; rho*_n = rho_n (1-rho_n)^{2^n - 1}; kappa_n = kappa_{n-1} rho*_n / 4; theta_n = tau_n = 2^{-2n-4} kappa_{n-1}; H(n) = ceiling(32 ln(3/theta_n) / (rho*_n tau_n)). Note kappa_n is decreasing and kappa_n <= rho*_n/4.
Partition omega into infinite sets J_n (n in omega). Partition each J_n into sets c(n,pi,beta), pi in omega, beta in 2^n, each of size r_n. Put R_n(pi,beta) = {w : w(i)=1 for all i in c(n,pi,beta)} and E_n(pi,beta) = R_n(pi,beta) minus the union of R_n(pi,beta') over beta' != beta. These sets are clopen. For fixed (n,pi) the sets E_n(pi,beta), beta in 2^n, are pairwise disjoint. lambda(E_n(pi,beta)) = rho*_n. For fixed n and beta the events E_n(pi,beta), pi in omega, are mutually independent, because E_n(pi,beta) depends only on the coordinates in c(n,pi) = union over beta' of c(n,pi,beta'), and these sets are disjoint for distinct pi. Also lambda(union over beta of R_n(pi,beta)) <= 2^n rho_n.

Step 2 (decoding and phi). For f in omega^omega and w in 2^omega let Sg(f,w) = {n : w in E_n(f(n),beta) for some beta in 2^n}; for n in Sg(f,w) let pay_n(f,w) be that unique beta. Say Delta(f,w) = a if Sg(f,w) is infinite and pay_n(f,w) is an initial segment of a for all but finitely many n in Sg(f,w). Such a is unique since pay_n has length n. The domain D of Delta is Borel and Delta is Borel on D, because 'w in E_n(f(n),beta)' is a clopen condition on (f,w). Define phi(f,w) = Psi(Delta(f,w), w) on D and 0^omega off D. phi is Borel. Since sum_n 2^n rho_n < infinity, Borel-Cantelli gives that N_f = {w : Sg(f,w) infinite} is a null Borel set, and phi_f = 0^omega off N_f.

Step 3 (Chernoff count). Let (Omega,nu) be a probability space, A a finite set, (E_pi : pi in A) mutually independent events of probability rho, and T a measurable set with nu(T) > 0 and nu(T cap E_pi) < (1/2) rho nu(T) for all pi in A. Then |A| <= 32 ln(3/nu(T)) / rho. Proof: let Z = sum of the indicators, mu = rho|A|. Integrating over T gives int_T Z < (1/2) mu nu(T), so by Markov nu(T cap {Z >= (3/4)mu}) < (2/3) nu(T), hence nu(Z < (3/4) mu) > nu(T)/3. The Chernoff lower-tail bound nu(Z <= (1-delta)mu) <= exp(-delta^2 mu/2) with delta = 1/4 gives nu(T)/3 < exp(-mu/32).

Step 4 (main lemma). Let P be a closed subset of 2^omega with lambda(P) > 0 and let a be in 2^omega. Then there is S with S(n) a subset of omega, |S(n)| <= H(n) for all n, such that for every f with f(n) not in S(n) for infinitely many n there is w in P with Delta(f,w) = a.
Proof. For each n write 2^omega = U_n x V_n with U_n = 2^{J_0 cup ... cup J_{n-1}} and V_n = 2^{J_n cup J_{n+1} cup ...}, with product measures mu_n, nu_n. For u in U_n let P_u = {v : (u,v) in P}. Each E_n(pi,beta) depends only on J_n, so it is a subset of V_n. Put beta_n = a|n and
 Low_n = {u : nu_n(P_u) < theta_n},
 Bad_n(pi) = {u : nu_n(P_u) >= theta_n and nu_n(P_u cap E_n(pi,beta_n)) < (1/2) rho*_n nu_n(P_u)}.
These are Borel (Fubini). By Step 3 applied in (V_n,nu_n) to T = P_u, each u lies in Bad_n(pi) for at most 32 ln(3/theta_n)/rho*_n values of pi. Integrating, sum over pi of mu_n(Bad_n(pi)) <= 32 ln(3/theta_n)/rho*_n. Let S(n) = {pi : mu_n(Bad_n(pi)) > tau_n}. Then |S(n)| <= H(n).
Now fix f with f(n) not in S(n) for infinitely many n. Fix n* >= 1 with 2^{-n*} <= lambda(P), and let n_1 < n_2 < ... enumerate all n >= n* with f(n) not in S(n). We build closed sets B_0 = 2^omega, B_1, B_2, ... , decreasing, with B_j determined by the coordinates in J_0 cup ... cup J_{n_j}, and show L_j := lambda(P cap B_j) >= lambda(P) kappa_{n_j} > 0.
Stage j >= 1, n = n_j, pi = f(n). Let Uns_j = {w : for every k with n_{j-1} < k < n (no k if j=1), w is in no R_k(f(k),beta)}; it is clopen, depends on coordinates in J_k with k < n, and lambda(complement of Uns_j) <= sum_{n_{j-1}<k<n} 2^k rho_k. Let Good = U_n minus (Low_n cup Bad_n(pi)) and choose a compact G'_j inside Good with mu_n(Good minus G'_j) <= tau_n. Put B_j = B_{j-1} cap Uns_j cap (G'_j x V_n) cap E_n(pi,beta_n). It is closed. Write B'' for the subset of U_n with B''x V_n = B_{j-1} cap Uns_j cap (G'_j x V_n) (possible since B_{j-1} depends on J_k, k <= n_{j-1} < n). By Fubini, L_j = integral over u in B'' of nu_n(P_u cap E_n(pi,beta_n)) >= (1/2) rho*_n integral over B'' of nu_n(P_u) = (1/2) rho*_n lambda(P cap (B'' x V_n)), because every u in B'' is in Good. Further lambda(P cap (B'' x V_n)) >= L_{j-1} - lambda(complement of Uns_j) - lambda(P cap (Low_n x V_n)) - mu_n(Bad_n(pi)) - mu_n(Good minus G'_j) >= L_{j-1} - sum_{n_{j-1}<k<n} 2^k rho_k - theta_n - 2 tau_n, using lambda(P cap (Low_n x V_n)) = integral over Low_n of nu_n(P_u) <= theta_n and pi not in S(n).
Estimate of the loss. For j = 1: the loss is theta_n + 2tau_n <= 3 * 2^{-2n-4} <= (3/16) 2^{-n} <= lambda(P)/2, so L_1 >= (1/2) rho*_n (lambda(P)/2) >= lambda(P) kappa_{n_1}. For j >= 2 let m = n_{j-1} >= n*. By the choice of r_k, 2^k rho_k <= 2^{-2k-4} kappa_{k-1} <= 2^{-2k-4} kappa_m for k > m, and theta_n = tau_n <= 2^{-2n-4} kappa_m. So the loss is at most kappa_m 4^{-m} (1/48 + 3/64) < kappa_m 4^{-m}/8 <= kappa_m lambda(P)/8 <= L_{j-1}/2 by the induction hypothesis L_{j-1} >= lambda(P) kappa_m. Hence L_j >= (rho*_n/4) L_{j-1} >= lambda(P) kappa_m rho*_n/4 >= lambda(P) kappa_{n_j}.
So the sets P cap B_j are nonempty, compact and decreasing; pick w in their intersection. Then w is in P. For every j, w is in E_{n_j}(f(n_j), a|n_j), so n_j is in Sg(f,w) with payload a|n_j. For k > n_1 not among the n_j, w is in Uns, so w is in no R_k(f(k),beta), hence k is not in Sg(f,w). So Sg(f,w) is infinite and all its members above n_1 have payload an initial segment of a. Thus Delta(f,w) = a.

Step 5 (hitting compact sets). Let K be compact in the plane with lambda^2(K) > 0, K = K_a. P = first projection of K is compact and lambda(P) >= lambda^2(K) > 0. Let S_K = S_{P,a} from Step 4. If f(n) is not in S_K(n) infinitely often, take w in P with Delta(f,w) = a; then phi_f(w) = Psi(a,w) is in K_w, so (w,phi_f(w)) is in K.

Step 6 (a small non-localized family). Fact A: for every null G and positive reals eps_n there are clopen D_n with lambda(D_n) <= eps_n and G contained in limsup D_n. Proof: take open O_m containing G with lambda(O_m) <= 2^{-m}; write each O_m as a disjoint union of cylinders; list all these cylinders (over all m) as c_1,c_2,...; the measures are summable and each point of G lies in infinitely many c_i. Choose i_0 < i_1 < ... with sum_{i >= i_n} lambda(c_i) <= eps_n and let D_n be the union of c_i for i_n <= i < i_{n+1}. 
Let (G_xi : xi < add(N)) be null sets with non-null union, let (C_i) enumerate the clopen sets, and put eps_n = 2^{-n}/H(n). By Fact A choose f_xi with lambda(C_{f_xi(n)}) <= eps_n and G_xi inside limsup_n C_{f_xi(n)}. If a slalom S with |S(n)| <= H(n) had f_xi(n) in S(n) for all but finitely many n, for every xi, then D*_n = union of {C_i : i in S(n), lambda(C_i) <= eps_n} has measure <= 2^{-n}, and the null set limsup D*_n would contain every G_xi, a contradiction. So F = {f_xi} is not localized by any such slalom.

Step 7 (conclusion). For every compact K of positive measure, some f in F escapes S_K infinitely often, so graph(phi_f) meets K by Step 5. A set meeting every compact set of positive measure is not null. Hence g <= |F| <= add(N). Conversely the graph of a Borel function is a Borel set with singleton sections, so it is lambda^2-null by Fubini, and fewer than add(N) null sets have a null union (add(N) is the same for the plane, which is measure-isomorphic to 2^omega). So g >= add(N).

Uses three facts quoted from Goto's paper via add-UN-note.md and context.md, not re-proved here: (F1) UN is invariant under Borel isomorphisms between uncountable Polish spaces; (F2) Goto's Claim 5.5.1: the graph of any function defined on a UN set is UN in the product; (F3) add(N) <= add(UN). For the 'in particular' part: Grzegorek's theorem (as quoted in context.md) gives a UN set of size non(N).

Let P be UN with |P| >= cof(N). Let (G_beta : beta < cof(N)) be a cofinal family of null Borel subsets of the plane (cof(N) for the plane equals cof(N)). For each beta choose a compact C_beta disjoint from G_beta with lambda^2(C_beta) > 0, and choose distinct points c_beta in P. Let F be the family of Claim 1, |F| <= add(N), and write phi_f for its functions.
For each beta the set K_beta = {(w, v + c_beta) : (w,v) in C_beta} is compact of positive measure (+ is coordinatewise addition mod 2). By Claim 1 choose f_beta in F and w_beta with (w_beta, phi_{f_beta}(w_beta)) in K_beta. Then q_beta := (w_beta, phi_{f_beta}(w_beta) + c_beta) is in C_beta.
For f in F let Gamma_f = {(w_beta, c_beta) : f_beta = f} and sigma_f(w,v) = (w, v + phi_f(w)). sigma_f is a Borel involution of the plane, and sigma_f[Gamma_f] = {q_beta : f_beta = f} =: W_f.
Gamma_f is UN: since the c_beta are distinct, Gamma_f is the coordinate swap of the graph of the function c_beta -> w_beta defined on a subset of P; subsets of UN sets are UN, so (F2) and (F1) apply. Hence W_f is UN by (F1).
The union of the W_f is {q_beta : beta < cof(N)}. It is not null: a null set is contained in some G_beta, but q_beta is in C_beta, which is disjoint from G_beta. A set that is not lambda^2-null is not UN. So add(N)-many (at most) UN sets have a non-UN union, giving add(UN) <= add(N). With (F3), add(UN) = add(N).
Remark: this is the argument of add-UN-note.md with two changes: the list of all compact sets is replaced by cof(N) of them, and the family of size d is replaced by the family of Claim 1.

claims.statement: Claim 3 (answers to Questions (1), (2), (4) of the task). (1) g = add(N) is provable, and add(N)-many partial Borel functions defined on null Borel sets can have graphs with non-null union. (2) g <= b, g <= non(M), g <= cov(M) and g <= add*(N) are all provable. (4) g > add(N) is not consistent; no lower bound above add(N) exists.
claims.proof:
(1) is Claim 1: the functions phi_f, f in F, restricted to the null Borel sets N_f = {w : Sg(f,w) infinite}, are partial Borel functions on null Borel domains. Off N_f the function phi_f is 0^omega, and the countably... more precisely the single horizontal line 2^omega x {0^omega} is null and compact K of positive measure minus this line still contains a compact set of positive measure, so the union of the partial graphs over N_f already meets every compact set of positive measure.
(2) follows from g = add(N) and the standard ZFC inequalities add(N) <= add(M) <= min(b, cov(M)), b <= non(M) (Cichon's diagram; quoted, not re-proved), and add(N) <= add*(N), which is immediate from the definition add*(N) = min{|X| : X + E is non-null for some null E} because X + E is a union of |X| null sets.
(4) is immediate from g = add(N).

claims.statement: Claim 4 (continuous and almost-everywhere variants). Let g_c be the least number of continuous functions 2^omega -> 2^omega whose graphs have non-null union. Let g* be the least size of a family of Borel functions f_xi such that no null Borel H in the plane satisfies lambda{w : (w,f_xi(w)) not in H} = 0 for all xi. Then (a) cov(M) <= g_c; (b) g <= g_c <= g*; (c) cov(M) <= g* <= non(N). Hence in the Cohen model (aleph_2 Cohen reals over a model of CH) g = aleph_1 while g_c = g* = c = aleph_2. (d) g* equals non(N) of the extension by one random real. So g is not, in general, non(N) of the one-random-real extension.
claims.proof:
Let Y be the space of sequences (C_k) of clopen subsets of the plane with lambda^2(C_k) <= 2^{-k}, a product of countable discrete spaces, so homeomorphic to omega^omega. For (C_k) in Y the set limsup C_k is null.
(a) Let (f_xi : xi < kappa) be continuous, kappa < cov(M). The graph of f_xi is compact and null, so for each n it is covered by one clopen set of measure <= 2^{-n}. Hence O_{xi,m} = {(C_k) : graph(f_xi) is contained in C_k for some k > m} is open and dense in Y. Fewer than cov(M) dense open subsets of a space homeomorphic to omega^omega have a common point (C_k). Then H = limsup C_k is null and contains every graph. So kappa < g_c.
(b) g <= g_c is trivial. For g_c <= g*: let (f_xi : xi < g*) witness g* (g* is infinite, since countably many graphs lie in one null set). By Lusin's theorem choose compact L_{xi,j} with lambda(L_{xi,j}) > 1 - 2^{-j} on which f_xi is continuous, and extend f_xi|L_{xi,j} to a continuous f_{xi,j} on 2^omega (a nonempty closed subset of 2^omega is a retract). If a null H contained all graphs of the f_{xi,j}, then (w,f_xi(w)) would be in H for all w in the conull set union_j L_{xi,j}, contradicting the choice. So the g* many continuous functions f_{xi,j} have graphs with non-null union.
(c) cov(M) <= g*: let (f_xi : xi < kappa) be Borel, kappa < cov(M). O_{xi,m,j} = {(C_k) : for some n > m, lambda{w : (w,f_xi(w)) in C_k for some m < k < n} > 1 - 2^{-j}} is open, and dense: given a finite initial segment C_0..C_{n-1} with n > m, take compact L with lambda(L) > 1 - 2^{-j} on which f_xi is continuous; graph(f_xi|L) is compact and null, so it lies in a clopen C_n of measure <= 2^{-n}. A common point (C_k) gives a null H = limsup C_k with (w,f_xi(w)) in H for almost every w, for every xi. So kappa < g*. g* <= non(N): for a non-null X take the constant functions f_x = x; if a null H had lambda(H^x) = 1 for all x in X (H^x the horizontal section), then X would lie in the null set {x : lambda(H^x) > 0}.
Cohen model: there non(M) = aleph_1 and cov(M) = c = aleph_2 (standard), so add(N) = aleph_1 and by Claim 1 g = aleph_1, while g_c, g* >= cov(M) = c.
(d) Sketch (confidence lower). Let r be random over V. Every real of V[r] is f(r) for a Borel f coded in V, and every null set of V[r] lies in H_r for a Borel H in V all of whose vertical sections are null (so H is null). If (f_xi) in V is almost covered by a null H in V, then r avoids the null set of w with H_w non-null and each null set {w : f_xi(w) not in H_w}, so {f_xi(r)} lies in the null set H_r; hence g* <= non(N)^{V[r]}. Conversely let (f_xi : xi < g*) witness g* and close it under f -> f o pi_{s,t}, where pi_{s,t} swaps the cylinders [s],[t] (|s|=|t|). If some positive-measure B forced {f(r)} null, there would be a null H with (w,f(w)) in H for almost all w in B, for all f in the closed family. Then H' = union over s,t of (pi_{s,t} x id)[H cap (B x 2^omega)] is null and almost covers each f_xi on the union of the sets pi_{s,t}[B], which is conull by the 0-1 law; contradiction. So the trivial condition forces the set {f(r)} to be non-null, giving non(N)^{V[r]} <= g*.

claims.statement: Claim 5 (Question (3)). With i(Psi) as in context.md (least size of a family of Borel sets N with (N+N) cap (Psi+Psi) = {0} whose union is non-null), every perfect Psi has i(Psi) >= add(N), and i(Psi_0) = add(N) for the closed perfect subgroup Psi_0 = {0} x 2^omega of 2^omega x 2^omega (identified with 2^omega by interleaving coordinates, a measure-preserving group isomorphism). So inf over perfect Psi of i(Psi) = add(N), and the infimum is attained. The proof does not use a Mycielski-type choice of Psi.
claims.proof:
Lower bound. Let N be Borel with (N+N) cap (Psi+Psi) = {0}. If lambda(N) > 0, then by Steinhaus N+N contains a neighbourhood of 0. Psi is perfect, so there are distinct a_n -> a in Psi, and a_n + a is a nonzero element of Psi+Psi converging to 0; so (N+N) cap (Psi+Psi) contains a nonzero point, a contradiction. Hence every such N is null, and a non-null union needs at least add(N) of them.
Upper bound. For Psi_0 = {0} x 2^omega we have Psi_0 + Psi_0 = Psi_0, and (N+N) cap Psi_0 = {(0,0)} holds iff no two distinct points of N have the same first coordinate, i.e. N is the graph of a partial function. The graphs of the Borel functions phi_f, f in F, of Claim 1 are such Borel sets, there are at most add(N) of them, and their union is non-null. So i(Psi_0) <= add(N).
Remark on the Mycielski idea in the task: for an add(N)-witness family (B_xi) the set union of (B_xi + B_xi) is in general not meagre (it can be all of 2^omega), so Mycielski's theorem does not apply directly; this route was not needed.

obstacles: Question 6.3 itself remains open in the case not covered by Claim 2: non(N) < cof(N) and no universally null set of size cof(N). The diagonal argument must meet cof(N) many compact sets with distinct points of one UN set, and a UN set has size at most non(N).

Attempt to remove the hypothesis, not completed: by Claim 1's decoding map, for each f the map Delta_f is Borel, and a set on which Delta_f is injective with UN image is UN. So add(UN) <= add(N) would follow from a UN set P, an injection p -> y_p with Delta_{f_p}(y_p) = p for suitable f_p in F, and {y_p : p in P} non-null. With |P| = non(N) < cof(N) I could not certify non-nullness; the natural Fubini-type certificate fails because the graph of a function from a UN set can lie inside a Borel set with null sections.
Since g = add(N), the bound add(UN) <= g cannot by itself separate add(UN) from add(N); it can only prove equality, and only under the size hypothesis on UN sets.

Literature not checked: only the arXiv abstract page of Bartoszynski-Roslanowski-Shelah, 'Adding one random real' (arXiv:math/9406229) was fetched; the PDF text could not be extracted in this environment, so its theorems and the Krawczyk/Pawlikowski attributions remain unverified. One web search found no earlier statement of g = add(N); Cichon-Pawlikowski and Pawlikowski's work on ideals of plane sets may contain related results and were not read.

Repair: cite Bartoszynski-Roslanowski-Shelah, 'Adding one random real', arXiv:math/9406229, Theorem 1.1(3) ('cov(N) >= b and non(N) <= d' in V^B, attributed there to Krawczyk) together with their Lemma 3.2 (non*(N) = non(N)^{V^B}); I read both in the PDF text. Claim 4(d) is a sketch, not a full proof. (i) It uses without proof the classical facts on names for reals and null sets in the random extension (BRS Lemma 1.2). (ii) The step 'the union of the sets pi_{s,t}[B] is conull by the 0-1 law' is not justified as written: the union over single swaps pi_{s,t} is not obviously invariant under finite coordinate changes, since a coordinate flip is a product of several swaps. The conclusion is true. Repair: by Lebesgue density pick s with lambda(B cap [s]) >= (1-eps) lambda([s]); then pi_{s,t}[B] has relative measure >= 1-eps in each [t], |t|=|s|. Or close the family and H' under the countable group generated by the swaps. (iii) The result is not new: it is BRS Lemma 3.2 (their non*(N), Definition 3.1, has an extra 'for all Borel non-null B' clause; the swap-closure argument shows it equals the submission's g*). It should be cited, not presented as newly argued.

attacks.summary:
Question 6.3 is NOT answered. No new ZFC upper bound for add(UN) below d was proved.

Proved:
- Strong-measure-zero witnesses cannot give ZFC bounds by b, d, cov(M) or add(M): under "c = aleph_2 and SN = [2^omega]^{<=aleph_1}" (consistent by GJS Thm 0.14) one has add(N) = add(UN) = b = d = cov(M) = aleph_1 < aleph_2 = add(SN) = add(SN,N) = non(N). So add(SN,N) <= d (hence <= b, <= cov(M), <= add(M)) is refuted, and add(UN) < add(SN) <= add(SN,N) is consistent. The value add(UN) = aleph_1 there uses the d-bound of add-UN-note.md (re-proved in Claim 3; I rechecked the Lemma line by line).
- BC implies cov(M) = aleph_1 and add(SN,N) = non(N). So any model of BC + non(N) > aleph_1 refutes add(SN,N) <= cov(M) (answer to the sample question: yes). Whether BC holds in the Mathias model was NOT verified, so I do not claim such a model; the GJS model already gives the refutation.
- New tools (all assume a UN set of size c): a fibred closure lemma for UN (Claim 1); a fibre principle replacing shears by arbitrary Borel maps (Claim 2); add(UN) <= theta for any theta < add(M) Borel sets with meager self-sums and non-null union, and add(UN) <= tau(C) = min{|X| : X + C not null} for every closed C with C + C nowhere dense, where cov(M) <= tau(C) <= non(N) (Claim 4).
- Trivial: add(UN) <= cov(UN) <= cov(SN) (Claim 6).

Status of the requested inequalities:
- add(UN) <= d: proved if a UN set of size c exists; open in ZFC.
- add(UN) <= b, <= cov(M), <= non(M), <= cov(N): open. Each follows from add(UN) = add(N); refuting any one would answer 6.3.
- add(SN,N) <= b, d, cov(M), add(M): refuted (consistently false).
- add(SN,N) <= cov(N), <= non(M): not decided. The GJS abstract adds a generalized Sierpinski set to its first model, which gives cov(N) = non(M) = c there. BC in the Mathias model would refute the cov(N) bound, but that is unchecked.

Two reductions that would be real progress: (a) a closed C with C+C nowhere dense and tau(C) = cov(M) gives add(UN) <= cov(M) under the hypothesis; (b) if add(N) < add(M) and add(N) Borel sets with meager self-sums have non-null union, then add(UN) = add(N) under the hypothesis. I could prove neither.
