claims.statement: Claim 1 (fibred closure of UN). Let Z be a Polish space, D a Borel subset of Z, f : D -> 2^omega a Borel map and W a subset of D. If f[W] is universally null and W ∩ f^{-1}{a} is universally null (in Z) for every a in 2^omega, then W is universally null in Z. In particular, if f restricted to W is injective and f[W] is UN, then W is UN. (This contains Goto's Claim 5.5.1 on graphs and the fact that a product of two UN sets is UN.)
claims.proof: Let mu be a finite atomless Borel measure on Z. Define nu(E) = mu(f^{-1}[E]) for Borel E ⊆ 2^omega; nu is a finite Borel measure on 2^omega. Let A_0 = {a : nu({a}) > 0}; A_0 is countable because nu is finite. Let nu'(E) = nu(E \ A_0). Then nu' is a finite Borel measure with no atoms. Since f[W] is UN, there is a Borel E ⊇ f[W] with nu'(E) = 0, that is mu(f^{-1}[E \ A_0]) = 0. Now W ⊆ f^{-1}[E \ A_0] ∪ ⋃_{a in A_0} (W ∩ f^{-1}{a}). The first set is mu-null. For each a in A_0 the set W ∩ f^{-1}{a} is UN in Z and mu is a finite atomless Borel measure on Z, so mu*(W ∩ f^{-1}{a}) = 0. A countable union of mu-null sets is mu-null, so mu*(W) = 0. As mu was arbitrary, W is UN. For the last sentence: if f restricted to W is injective, each W ∩ f^{-1}{a} has at most one point, hence is UN.

claims.statement: Claim 2 (fibre principle). Assume there is a universally null set P ⊆ 2^omega of cardinality c. Let Z be an uncountable Polish space with a finite atomless Borel measure lambda_Z, and let (pi_xi : xi < theta) be Borel maps pi_xi : D_xi -> 2^omega with Borel domains D_xi ⊆ Z. Suppose that for every p in P the set A_p = ⋃_{xi<theta} pi_xi^{-1}{p} is not lambda_Z-null. Then add(UN) <= theta. (The shear proof of add-UN-note.md is the case Z = 2^omega x 2^omega, pi_h(v,w) = v + w∘h.)
claims.proof: UN and add(UN) do not depend on the uncountable Polish space: a Borel isomorphism carries finite atomless Borel measures to finite atomless Borel measures, so it carries UN sets to UN sets. So it suffices to find theta UN subsets of Z whose union is not UN. There are exactly c lambda_Z-null G_delta subsets of Z; list them as (H_beta : beta < c). By recursion on beta < c choose p_beta in P \ {p_gamma : gamma < beta} (possible since |P| = c), then q_beta in A_{p_beta} \ H_beta (possible since A_{p_beta} is not null, so it is not contained in H_beta), then xi_beta < theta with q_beta in D_{xi_beta} and pi_{xi_beta}(q_beta) = p_beta. For xi < theta let W_xi = {q_beta : xi_beta = xi}. If q_beta = q_gamma and xi_beta = xi_gamma = xi, then p_beta = pi_xi(q_beta) = pi_xi(q_gamma) = p_gamma, so beta = gamma. Hence pi_xi restricted to W_xi is injective, and pi_xi[W_xi] ⊆ P is UN. By Claim 1, W_xi is UN. The union W = {q_beta : beta < c} is not lambda_Z-null: every null set is contained in some H_beta, and q_beta is not in H_beta. So W is not UN. Thus theta UN sets have a non-UN union, and add(UN) <= theta.

claims.statement: Claim 3 (re-derivation of the note's bound from Claim 2; not new). (a) Lemma S: if K ⊆ 2^omega x 2^omega is compact with lambda^2(K) > 0, there is F_K in omega^omega such that for every strictly increasing h with h(n) >= F_K(n) for all n there is w with (w∘h, w) in K. (b) If there is a UN set of size c, then add(UN) <= d.
claims.proof:
(a) By the Lebesgue density theorem pick m_0 and s_0, t_0 in 2^{m_0} with lambda^2(K ∩ [s_0]x[t_0]) >= (3/4) 4^{-m_0}; put K_0 = K ∩ [s_0]x[t_0]. For m >= m_0 let K^(m) be the union of the boxes [s]x[t], s,t in 2^m, that meet K_0. These clopen sets decrease to K_0 (K_0 is compact), so delta(m) := lambda^2(K^(m) \ K_0) -> 0, and delta(m_0) <= (1/4) 4^{-m_0} because K^(m_0) = [s_0]x[t_0]. Choose m_0 < m_1 < ... with delta(m_k) <= 8^{-k} 4^{-m_0} for k >= 1, and let F_K(n) = m_{n+1}. Fix a strictly increasing h with h(n) >= m_{n+1} for all n, and let gamma be the distribution of (w∘h, w) for lambda-random w. For s,t in 2^m let j = |{i < m : h(i) < m}|. The coordinates h(i), i < m, are distinct and m - j of them are >= m, hence independent of w restricted to m. So gamma([s]x[t]) <= 2^{-m} 2^{-(m-j)} = 2^j 4^{-m}, with equality if j = 0. At m = m_0 we have j = 0 since h(0) >= m_1 > m_0, so gamma(K^(m_0)) = 4^{-m_0}. At m = m_{k+1} we have j <= k, because h(i) >= m_{i+1} >= m_{k+1} for i >= k. The set K^(m_k) \ K^(m_{k+1}) is a union of depth-m_{k+1} boxes contained in K^(m_k) \ K_0, so its lambda^2-measure is at most delta(m_k) and gamma(K^(m_k) \ K^(m_{k+1})) <= 2^k delta(m_k). Hence gamma(K_0) >= 4^{-m_0} - delta(m_0) - sum_{k>=1} 2^k 8^{-k} 4^{-m_0} >= 4^{-m_0}(1 - 1/4 - 1/3) > 0. So some (w∘h, w) lies in K_0 ⊆ K.
(b) Fix a family D of d strictly increasing functions such that every F in omega^omega is pointwise below some h in D (close a dominating family of size d under finite modifications, then replace g by n -> max_{i<=n} g(i) + n). Let Z = 2^omega x 2^omega with lambda^2 and pi_h(v,w) = v + w∘h for h in D (continuous). Then pi_h^{-1}{p} = {(p + w∘h, w) : w}, so A_p = (p,0) + G with G = ⋃_{h in D} {(w∘h, w) : w}. By (a), G meets every compact set of positive measure, so G is not null (the complement of a null G_delta contains a compact set of positive measure). Translation preserves lambda^2, so A_p is not null for every p. Claim 2 with theta = d gives add(UN) <= d.

claims.statement: Claim 4 (meager self-sum form). Assume there is a UN set of size c. (a) If (B_xi : xi < theta) are Borel subsets of 2^omega with non-null union and Q is a perfect set with (B_xi + B_xi) ∩ (Q + Q) ⊆ {0} for every xi, then add(UN) <= theta. (b) If theta < add(M) and (B_xi : xi < theta) are Borel sets with non-null union such that each B_xi + B_xi is meager, then add(UN) <= theta. (c) If C ⊆ 2^omega is closed and C + C is nowhere dense, then add(UN) <= tau(C) := min{|X| : X + C is not null}. (d) Without any hypothesis: for every closed null C, cov(M) <= tau(C) <= non(N). Consequence of (b): if add(N) < add(M) and some family of add(N) Borel sets with meager self-sums has a non-null union, then add(UN) = add(N) (given a UN set of size c).
claims.proof:
Mycielski-type lemma (proved here for completeness): if R ⊆ 2^omega x 2^omega is meager, there is a perfect Q with (q,q') not in R for all distinct q,q' in Q. Proof: write R ⊆ ⋃_n R_n with R_n closed nowhere dense and increasing. Build nonempty clopen sets U_s, s in 2^{<omega}, with U_{s0}, U_{s1} disjoint subsets of U_s, diam(U_s) <= 2^{-|s|}, and (U_s x U_t) ∩ R_n = ∅ for distinct s,t in 2^n. At step n, first split each U_s into two disjoint nonempty clopen pieces, then treat the finitely many ordered pairs of distinct pieces (V,V') one at a time: V x V' is nonempty open and R_n is closed nowhere dense, so there are nonempty clopen V_1 ⊆ V, V'_1 ⊆ V' with (V_1 x V'_1) ∩ R_n = ∅; shrink V, V' to V_1, V'_1. Let Q = ⋂_n ⋃_{|s|=n} U_s. Q is perfect. Distinct q,q' in Q lie in U_s x U_t with s ≠ t in 2^n for all large n, so (q,q') is in no R_n.
(a) Q is compact, perfect and zero-dimensional, so there is a homeomorphism phi : 2^omega -> Q. If P' is UN of size c then P = phi[P'] is UN: for a finite atomless Borel mu on 2^omega, nu(E) = mu(phi[E]) is finite atomless Borel, nu*(P') = 0, and the image of a nu-null Borel cover is a mu-null Borel cover of P. So P ⊆ Q is UN of size c. For each xi the map (b,q) -> b + q is injective on B_xi x Q: b + q = b' + q' gives b + b' = q + q' in (B_xi + B_xi) ∩ (Q + Q) ⊆ {0}, so b = b' and q = q'. By the Lusin-Souslin theorem (an injective Borel image of a Borel set is Borel and the inverse is Borel; standard, quoted from memory) D_xi = B_xi + Q is Borel and pi_xi : D_xi -> Q, pi_xi(b + q) = q, is Borel. For p in P, pi_xi^{-1}{p} = B_xi + p, so A_p = p + ⋃_xi B_xi, which is not null. Claim 2 with Z = 2^omega gives add(UN) <= theta.
(b) Addition s(q,q') = q + q' is a continuous open surjection of (2^omega)^2 onto 2^omega, so R_xi = s^{-1}[B_xi + B_xi] is meager. Since theta < add(M) (the same cardinal for the square), R = ⋃_xi R_xi is meager. The lemma gives a perfect Q with q + q' not in B_xi + B_xi for distinct q,q' in Q and all xi. Since q + q' = 0 iff q = q', this says (B_xi + B_xi) ∩ (Q + Q) ⊆ {0}. Apply (a).
(c) Let X have size tau(C) with X + C not null, and B_x = x + C for x in X. Then B_x + B_x = C + C for every x, so the single relation R = s^{-1}[C + C] is closed nowhere dense. The lemma gives Q with (C + C) ∩ (Q + Q) ⊆ {0}. Apply (a) with theta = tau(C).
(d) Upper bound: if X is not null, X + C ⊇ X + c_0 is not null. Lower bound: let Y be the product over n of the countable discrete set of clopen subsets of 2^omega of measure < 2^{-n}; Y is homeomorphic to omega^omega. For y in Y let H_y = ⋂_m ⋃_{n>=m} y(n); lambda(H_y) = 0. For a compact null K the set D_K = {y : for all m there is n >= m with K ⊆ y(n)} is a dense G_delta: given a finite initial segment of y of length k and m, take n >= max(k,m) and a clopen U ⊇ K of measure < 2^{-n} (K is compact and null) and put y(n) = U. If |X| < cov(M), choose y in ⋂_{x in X} D_{x+C}. Then X + C ⊆ H_y is null. So tau(C) >= cov(M).
Consequence: add(N) <= add(UN) always; (b) with theta = add(N) gives the reverse inequality.

claims.statement: Claim 5 (strong measure zero witnesses give no ZFC bound by d, b, cov(M), add(M)). ZFC proves: if c = aleph_2 and SN = [2^omega]^{<=aleph_1}, then add(SN) = add(SN,N) = non(N) = aleph_2 and add(N) = add(UN) = b = d = cov(M) = aleph_1. The hypothesis is consistent by Goldstern-Judah-Shelah, arXiv:math/9306214v1, Theorem 0.14 (fetched and read). Hence ZFC does not prove add(SN,N) <= d, and add(UN) < add(SN) <= add(SN,N) is consistent.
claims.proof:
Assume c = aleph_2 and SN = [2^omega]^{<=aleph_1}.
(1) Every set of size aleph_1 is SMZ, hence null. So non(N) = aleph_2 = c.
(2) A union of aleph_1 sets of size <= aleph_1 has size <= aleph_1, so it is SMZ and null. So add(SN) >= aleph_2 and add(SN,N) >= aleph_2. Also add(SN) <= add(SN,N) <= non(N) = aleph_2 (singletons of a non-null set of size non(N)).
(3) d = aleph_1. Suppose d = c. List omega^omega as (g_j : j < c) and choose f_i with f_i not <=* g_j for all j < i (possible: fewer than d functions are not dominating). Then for each j, {i : f_i <=* g_j} ⊆ {i : i <= j} has size <= aleph_1; in particular each value is taken by at most aleph_1 indices, so {f_i} has size aleph_2. Let F(f) = 0^{f(0)} 1 0^{f(1)} 1 ... . F is a homeomorphism of omega^omega onto R = {x : x(n) = 1 infinitely often}, and 2^omega \ R = {r_n : n in omega} is countable. Let X = {F(f_i) : i < c}; |X| = aleph_2. X is SMZ: given h in omega^omega, U_1 = ⋃_n [r_n restricted to h(2n)] is open and contains 2^omega \ R, so K = 2^omega \ U_1 is a compact subset of R, F^{-1}[K] is compact, hence pointwise bounded by some g. So X \ U_1 ⊆ {F(f_i) : f_i <= g} has size <= aleph_1, is SMZ, and is covered by cylinders of lengths h(2n+1). Together X is covered by cylinders of lengths h(n). This contradicts SN ⊆ [2^omega]^{<=aleph_1}. So d < c, that is d = aleph_1. (This is the argument of GJS 0.11-0.13, moved to 2^omega.)
(4) aleph_1 <= add(N) <= b <= d and cov(M) <= d (standard), so all are aleph_1.
(5) add(UN) = aleph_1: by (1) and Grzegorek's theorem (as quoted in Goto's paper) there is a UN set of size non(N) = c. Claim 3(b) gives add(UN) <= d = aleph_1, and add(UN) >= add(N) >= aleph_1.
Consistency: GJS Theorem 0.14 states verbatim that 'ZFC + c = aleph_2 + S = [IR]^{<=aleph_1} + there are no Cohen reals over L is consistent', and notes that this implies Add(S) and b = d = aleph_1. Transfer from IR to 2^omega (GJS Remark 0.2(b)): let e : 2^omega -> [0,1] be binary expansion. It maps a cylinder of length n into an interval of length 2^{-n} and is at most 2-to-1; an interval of length <= 2^{-m} is covered by two closed dyadic intervals of level m, whose preimages are cylinders of length m plus at most two points each. So X ⊆ 2^omega is SMZ iff e[X] is SMZ (countable sets are SMZ), and |X| <= aleph_1 iff |e[X]| <= aleph_1. Hence S = [IR]^{<=aleph_1} gives SN = [2^omega]^{<=aleph_1}.
Conclusion: in that model add(SN,N) = aleph_2 > aleph_1 = d >= b, cov(M), add(M), and add(UN) = aleph_1 < aleph_2 = add(SN).

claims.statement: Claim 6 (elementary facts). (a) add(UN) <= cov(UN) <= cov(SN), and add(SN,N) <= cov(SN). (b) The Borel Conjecture implies cov(M) = aleph_1 and add(SN,N) = non(N). Hence every model of BC + non(N) > aleph_1 satisfies add(SN,N) > cov(M). (c) Under 'c = aleph_2, SN = [2^omega]^{<=aleph_1} and there is a generalized Sierpinski set' one has cov(N) = non(M) = c, so that model does not refute add(SN,N) <= cov(N) or add(SN,N) <= non(M).
claims.proof:
(a) A family in an ideal I that covers 2^omega has a union outside N and outside UN, so add(I,N) <= cov(I) and add(I) <= cov(I). SN ⊆ UN gives cov(UN) <= cov(SN). (SN ⊆ UN: for a finite atomless Borel mu on the compact space 2^omega and eps > 0 there is n with mu([s]) < eps for all s in 2^n, by compactness and atomlessness; so an SMZ set has mu-outer measure 0.)
(b) Every X with |X| < cov(M) is SMZ: for h in omega^omega and x in X the set {sigma in prod_n 2^{h(n)} : sigma(n) = x restricted to h(n) for some n} is dense open, and fewer than cov(M) dense open sets have a common point sigma; then X ⊆ ⋃_n [sigma(n)]. Under BC a set of size aleph_1 is not SMZ, so cov(M) <= aleph_1. Under BC, SN is the ideal of countable sets; kappa countable sets have a union of size <= kappa·aleph_0, so a non-null union needs kappa >= non(N), and non(N) singletons suffice. So add(SN,N) = non(N).
(c) Let S be a generalized Sierpinski set: |S| = c = aleph_2 and every null set meets S in fewer than c points. If 2^omega were a union of aleph_1 null sets, S would have size <= aleph_1. So cov(N) = aleph_2. Rothberger's inequality cov(N) <= non(M) gives non(M) = aleph_2. (The GJS abstract lists 'there is a generalized Sierpinski set' with its first model; I did not read that part of the paper.)

obstacles: Question 6.3 remains open. None of add(UN) <= b, <= cov(M), <= non(M), <= cov(N) was proved or refuted. Each follows from add(UN) = add(N), so a refutation of any one would itself answer 6.3.

All new tools (Claims 2-4) still need a UN set of size c. Without it the recursion cannot meet cof(N) many null sets with only non(N) points; Lemma B of context.md does not obviously repair this when non(N) < c.

Category cannot replace domination in a Borel-uniform family. If pi(z,y) is jointly Borel and Y is non-meager, then {p : the set of z with {y : pi(z,y) = p} non-meager has positive measure} is a Borel set that is null for every atomless measure, hence countable. So a non-meager index set helps for only countably many p. This blocks a direct proof of add(UN) <= non(M) by the fibre principle.

For a closed subgroup Q the cardinal from Claim 4(a) is exactly the note's g (Lusin-Novikov), so nothing below g is gained. For the non-group perfect set Q of branches of 2^{<omega}, a domain M separates Q only if it blocks percolation, which forces M to be thick; the sparse-domain lemma then fails. A random density-1/2 set M does separate Q (critical Galton-Watson dies out), but the resulting fibred sets again reduce to g.

Sets with meager self-sum that I could construct are all in the sigma-ideal E generated by closed null sets, where the lower bound is cov(M) (Claim 4(d)). Limsup-type null sets, which witness add(N), always have comeager self-sum. I could not decide whether add(N) many Borel sets with meager self-sum can have a non-null union.

Whether some closed C with C + C nowhere dense has tau(C) = cov(M) (or even tau(C) <= d) is open to me. Subgroups {u : u restricted to A = 0} give tau = non(N). I recall a Bartoszynski-Shelah theorem add(E,N) = cov(M); this is from memory and NOT checked, and its witnesses would have to be translates of one such C to apply Claim 4(c).
Bounded eventually-different families do not help: min over bounded b of the eventually-different covering number is non(SN) (Rothberger), which is aleph_2 > cov(M) in the GJS model.

Not verified: that the Borel Conjecture holds in the Mathias model. GKSW (arXiv:1105.0823, fetched) states the two ingredients only for Laver forcing. If BC holds there, then add(SN,N) = non(N) = aleph_2 > cov(N) = cov(M) = aleph_1 in that model, which would also refute add(SN,N) <= cov(N). The status of add(SN,N) <= non(M) is unknown to me.

Not verified: whether g = aleph_1 in the Cohen model, and whether g <= non(M) or g >= cov(M) hold in ZFC. A heuristic computation suggests g = aleph_1 < cov(M) in the Cohen model, but I have no proof.

Mycielski's theorem and the Lusin-Souslin theorem are quoted from memory (the first is proved in Claim 4; the second is standard descriptive set theory). Claim 5 depends on the unrefereed d-bound of add-UN-note.md, re-proved as Claim 3; no human expert has checked it.

referees.notes:
Referee 1, finished 20:42 EST. I found no false claim and no step that needs a new idea. The submission is honestly labelled: Question 6.3 is not answered, and every bound proved is either conditional on a UN set of size c or a computation in one model.

WHAT I CHECKED, CLAIM BY CLAIM

Claim 1 (fibred closure). Correct. The pushforward nu is a finite Borel measure, its atom set A_0 is countable, and nu' = nu restricted off A_0 has no point masses. W is covered by f^{-1}[E \ A_0] plus countably many fibres. The two corollaries (Goto's Claim 5.5.1, products of UN sets) follow.

Claim 2 (fibre principle). Correct. The recursion has length c and uses only |P| = c and "A_p is not contained in a null G_delta". This is outer measure only; no Fubini step and no measurability of A_p is used.
- Wording slip: the sentence "If q_beta = q_gamma ... so beta = gamma. Hence pi_xi restricted to W_xi is injective" argues the converse. The correct line is: pi_xi(q_beta) = p_beta and the p_beta are pairwise distinct, so pi_xi(q_beta) = pi_xi(q_gamma) gives beta = gamma. The conclusion holds.

Claim 3 (Lemma S and add(UN) <= d given a UN set of size c). Correct. I rechecked every estimate:
- gamma([s]x[t]) is 0 or 2^{-(2m-j)}, because the constrained coordinates are m + (m-j) distinct ones.
- j = 0 at depth m_0, and j <= k at depth m_{k+1}.
- K^(m_k) \ K^(m_{k+1}) is a union of depth-m_{k+1} boxes of total lambda^2-measure <= delta(m_k). So its gamma-measure is <= 2^k delta(m_k), including k = 0.
- The sum gives gamma(K_0) >= (5/12) 4^{-m_0} > 0.
- The family D is correctly built (everywhere-dominating, strictly increasing, size d).
- The direction agrees with what I recall of the known fact non(N) <= d after one random real (recalled, not fetched).

Claim 4. Correct.
- Mycielski lemma: the proof is complete (increasing closed nowhere dense R_n, fusion of clopen sets).
- (a): b+q = b'+q' gives b+b' = q+q' in {0}. Lusin-Souslin is used correctly; it is a textbook theorem, cited by name only.
- (b): addition is a continuous open surjection, so preimages of meager sets are meager, and theta < add(M) keeps the union meager.
- (c): C + C is compact nowhere dense, so its preimage is closed nowhere dense.
- (d): D_K is a dense G_delta in a copy of omega^omega, and X + C lies in H_y. This agrees with add(E,N) = cov(M) as I recall it (not fetched).
- Degenerate case: (c) and (d) need C nonempty.

Claim 5. Correct.
- Steps (1)-(5) are valid ZFC arguments. add(SN) <= add(SN,N) holds because a non-null union is not SMZ.
- Step (3) reproduces GJS 0.11-0.13 on 2^omega.
- I fetched arXiv:math/9306214v1 myself. The arXiv record gives the title "Strong measure zero sets without Cohen reals" and authors Goldstern, Judah, Shelah. Theorem 0.14 reads as quoted, and the note after it says that c = aleph_2 and S = [IR]^{<=aleph_1} imply Add(S) and b = d = aleph_1 "by 0.11". Remark 0.2(b) and 0.11-0.13 are as described.
- The transfer from IR to 2^omega by binary expansion is correct.
- Grzegorek's theorem is quoted in Goto's paper as stated (confirmed in flat.txt, intro and Proposition 6.4).

Claim 6. Correct.
- (a) is trivial. SN is contained in UN by the Konig-type compactness argument.
- (b) is right. If some h(n) = 0 the cover is trivial, so assume h(n) >= 1.
- (c) is right. Better citation: GJS Theorem 0.15 (page 4 of v1) states the model with c = aleph_2, S = [IR]^{<=aleph_1}, no Cohen reals over L and a generalized Sierpinski set. The author need not rely on the abstract.

TESTS AGAINST MODELS

- Every new inequality is an upper bound that is >= add(N) (families of fewer than add(N) null sets have null union; a single positive-measure B is excluded by Steinhaus). So none can contradict a model where add(UN) = add(N), and no model with add(N) < add(UN) is known.
- MA: d = c and the hypotheses of 4(b) are vacuous.
- Cohen, Hechler: non(N) = c, add(UN) = aleph_1 by Theorem 5.18; consistent.
- Random: non(N) = aleph_1; consistent.
- Laver, Mathias, Miller: d = c, so Claim 3 gives nothing new there.
- GJS model: d = aleph_1 < non(N) = c. Claim 3 gives a union of aleph_1 closed null sets of full outer measure. This is consistent with cov(M) <= d and with cov(N) = aleph_2 in the 0.15 model. It does not conflict with Theorem 5.18, since GJS use a countable support iteration.
- The refutation of add(SN,N) <= d, b, cov(M), add(M) stands.

NOT VERIFIED BY ME

- The forcing proof of GJS Theorem 0.14/0.15 (their Section 3). I verified only that the theorem is stated.
- Grzegorek's original paper.
- Whether BC holds in the Mathias model. The author also leaves this open and claims nothing from it. The first 5 pages of arXiv:1105.0823 (title "Borel Conjecture and dual Borel Conjecture", Goldstern, Kellner, Shelah, Wohofsky; fetched) do not mention the Mathias model.

NOVELTY

- Claim 4(a) is the same as "tool 3" (independent-set form) in context.md.
- Claim 2 is a mild generalisation of condition (‡) and the shear proof.
- Claim 3 is the note's theorem.
- Genuinely added: the Mycielski step in 4(b),(c), the tau(C) bounds, and the Claim 5 model computation separating add(UN) from add(SN) and add(SN,N).
